title: Biomarkers in Patients With Acute Ischaemic Stroke Undergoing Thrombectomy Compared With Controls: A Pilot Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Detection of cerebral ischaemia is challenging in patients who are anaesthetised, sedated or have reduced levels of consciousness, as neurological examination is difficult or even impossible to assess. Furthermore, as some patients cannot be transported for radiology, for example during surgery, a reliable blood biomarker for detecting acute cerebral events would be of considerable clinical value. We aimed to compare levels of brain injury biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and total tau (tau) in patients with acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy under general anaesthesia or sedation to controls undergoing non-cerebral surgery under general anaesthesia. These biomarkers were chosen because previous studies have demonstrated their potential as blood biomarkers of acute cerebral injury and ischaemic stroke.

METHODS: In this prospective, observational pilot study, conducted at the Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg, Sweden, between 2021 and 2024, GFAP, NfL, and tau were analysed using the Simoa Neurology 4-plex assay, before thrombectomy or surgery and at 2- and 24 h thereafter.

RESULTS: Blood samples from 21 patients with AIS and 19 controls were analysed. GFAP concentrations in patients with AIS increased significantly from baseline to 24 h (median 301.0 → 1443.0 pg/mL; p = 0.001) and were higher than in controls at all time points (p < 0.01). In the controls there was no significant increase in GFAP from baseline to 24 h (p = 0.449). NfL and tau increased significantly in patients with AIS (p = 0.001 and 0.002) but also in the controls (p = 0.001 and 0.047).

CONCLUSION: GFAP and NfL concentrations were higher in patients with acute ischaemic stroke than in surgical controls at all sampling time points, whereas tau differed only after 24 h. Unlike NfL and tau, GFAP did not increase significantly in controls, suggesting that it may be less influenced by anaesthesia and surgery. These findings support further evaluation of GFAP as a potential biomarker of acute cerebral injury in perioperative and critical care settings.

EDITORIAL COMMENT: A biomarker of ischaemic cerebral injury could be attractive to support treatments to protect brain health during anaesthesia and surgery. In a pilot study, glial fibrillary acidic protein emerged as a potential candidate as it was increased in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy for large-vessel ischaemic stroke compared to anaesthetised patients undergoing non-cerebral surgery.

title: Individualised Versus Conventional Balloon Dilation for TIPS: Hepatic Encephalopathy in a Propensity-Matched Before-After Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatic encephalopathy (HE) is a major complication of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS). Stent under-dilation reduces HE, but a fixed diameter cannot be individualised to patient risk. An individualised scoring system tailoring balloon diameter to patient characteristics, without compromising efficacy or increasing variceal re-bleeding or stent dysfunction, is needed.

METHODS: In this retrospective study, 717 patients with cirrhosis underwent TIPS with 8-mm covered stents between December 2015 and December 2023. Patients received conventional 8-mm full dilation (n = 408; before December 1, 2020) or individualised dilation (n = 309; from December 1, 2020 onward), with the balloon diameter (5-7 mm) chosen by an 11-factor scoring system. The primary endpoint was overt HE (West Haven grade II-IV) within 6 months. Propensity score matching, inverse probability weighting, Fine-Grey and E-value analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Six-month overt HE was lower in the individualised group (14.6%; 45 of 309) than in the conventional group (27.5%; 112 of 408), yielding an absolute risk reduction of 12.9 percentage points (number needed to treat, 8; p < 0.001). After propensity score matching on 18 covariates (259 pairs), the conditional odds ratio was 0.42 (95% CI, 0.27-0.66; p < 0.001), consistent with inverse probability weighting (odds ratio, 0.47). Six-month re-bleeding (1.5% vs. 1.3%), stent dysfunction (3.9% vs. 4.2%) and ascites improvement (61.0% vs. 62.1%) did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSIONS: An individualised balloon dilation strategy incorporating an 11-factor scoring system was associated with reduced post-TIPS HE, with no clear difference in variceal re-bleeding, stent dysfunction or ascites recurrence.

title: SLC3A2 Silencing Alleviates Aortic Dissection via cAMP-PKA Activation and Disulfidptosis Inhibition.
abstract: Aortic dissection (AD) is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Disulfidptosis, a novel disulfide stress-induced cell death, remains unexplored in AD. We investigated whether solute carrier family 3 member 2 (SLC3A2), a disulfidptosis-related gene, contributes to AD pathogenesis. Bioinformatic analyses of Gene Expression Omnibus datasets combined machine learning algorithms to identify SLC3A2 as a core gene. A murine AD model was established using β-aminopropionitrile and angiotensin II, with lentiviral knockdown of SLC3A2. Human aortic vascular smooth muscle cells (HAVSMCs) were challenged with BAY-876 to induce disulfidptosis. Histological staining evaluated medial degeneration and elastic fiber integrity. Disulfidptosis was assessed by measuring cystine accumulation and the protein expression of filamin A (FLNA) and NCK-associated protein 1 (NCKAP1). The involvement of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP)-protein kinase A (PKA) signaling was verified by genetic knockdown of its catalytic subunit (PRKACA). We observed SLC3A2 was upregulated in AD. SLC3A2 knockdown delayed lethal aortic rupture, reduced aortic medial degeneration, decreased reactive oxygen species and cystine, while restoring glutathione and free thiols. In HAVSMCs, SLC3A2 silencing preserved filamentous actin integrity, reversed the BAY-876-induced downregulation of α-smooth muscle actin and smooth muscle 22 alpha, and restored the aberrant expression of FLNA and NCKAP1. Mechanistically, SLC3A2 knockdown reactivated the cAMP-PKA signaling axis suppressed by BAY-876, and PRKACA knockdown abrogated the protective effects of SLC3A2 silencing on oxidative stress, cytoskeletal integrity, and disulfidptosis. In conclusion, SLC3A2 drives AD progression by suppressing cAMP-PKA signaling, thereby exacerbating oxidative stress and disulfidptotic cytoskeletal collapse. Targeting the SLC3A2/cAMP-PKA axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy for AD.

We investigated whether solute carrier family 3 member 2 (SLC3A2), a disulfidptosis-related gene, contributes to AD pathogenesis.

title: Left vertebral artery dissecting aneurysm compressing the cervical nerve roots and mimicking cervical radiculopathy: a case report.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vertebral artery dissection usually presents with head and neck pain or posterior circulation ischemia. In rare cases, a dissecting aneurysm or focal arterial dilatation may compress adjacent cervical nerve roots or the upper trunk of the brachial plexus, thereby mimicking cervical radiculopathy.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 54-year-old woman presented with an 8-day history of head and neck pain and a 4-day history of progressive weakness of the left upper limb. Neurological examination suggested involvement of the left C5-C6 nerve roots or the upper trunk of the brachial plexus. Conventional imaging of the cervical spine and shoulder identified degenerative and musculoskeletal abnormalities; however, these findings did not adequately explain the rapidly progressive proximal weakness. Magnetic resonance imaging of the brachial plexus demonstrated relative enlargement and increased signal intensity of the left C5 nerve root compared with the contralateral side. Targeted color Doppler ultrasonography revealed focal dilatation of the left vertebral artery with suspected dissection-related changes and compression of adjacent neural structures. Electrodiagnostic testing supported involvement of the left C5-C6 nerve roots or the upper trunk of the brachial plexus, and digital subtraction angiography confirmed a left vertebral artery dissecting aneurysm. The patient subsequently underwent reconstructive endovascular stent treatment. Her neck and shoulder pain improved markedly after treatment, and the strength of the left upper limb gradually recovered.

CONCLUSION: Vertebral artery dissection associated with a dissecting aneurysm and neural compression should be considered in patients presenting with acute or subacute neck and shoulder pain accompanied by progressive proximal upper-limb weakness, particularly when common cervical spine, shoulder, or peripheral nerve disorders do not adequately explain the neurological localization or clinical course.

In rare cases, a dissecting aneurysm or focal arterial dilatation may compress adjacent cervical nerve roots or the upper trunk of the brachial plexus, thereby mimicking cervical radiculopathy. CASE PRESENTATION: A 54-year-old woman presented with an 8-day history of head and neck pain and a 4-day history of progressive weakness of the left upper limb.

title: Association between the platelet to lymphocyte ratio and the clinical outcome of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate the association between platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio and clinical outcomes in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. Study quality was assessed using appropriate tools, and pooled estimates were calculated using a random-effects model with sensitivity and subgroup analyses. Ten studies involving patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage were included. The meta-analysis showed that a higher platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio was associated with an increased likelihood of poor functional outcome. In contrast, no clear association was observed between platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio and delayed cerebral ischemia in the pooled analysis. The odds ratios for pneumonia and deep vein thrombosis each came from a single independent study rather than from pooled meta-analytic analyses; these unpooled estimates therefore remain exploratory and should not be interpreted as combined effect sizes. Substantial heterogeneity was present across analyses, and sensitivity analyses suggested that the results for functional outcome and delayed cerebral ischemia were not entirely stable. The available evidence is limited by the small number of studies, heterogeneity in threshold values and outcome definitions, and geographic concentration of the included populations. In conclusion, the platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio may serve as a readily available prognostic marker in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, but current evidence is insufficient to support its routine clinical use. Further large, well-designed multinational studies are needed to establish optimal thresholds and to clarify its incremental value in prognostic assessment.

title: A pseudo-ischemic tumor ecosystem couples malignant stress and inflammatory myeloid remodeling across adenocarcinomas.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer-associated thrombosis and tumor immune remodeling may converge through hypoxia, myeloid inflammation, neutrophil extracellular traps, platelet engagement, and endothelial dysfunction. We investigated whether they define a conserved, transcriptomically measurable tumor state.

METHODS: We integrated a lung adenocarcinoma extracellular-vesicle RNA dataset with three venous thromboembolism cohorts to derive five immunothrombotic modules. Single-cell RNA-sequencing data from lung (LUAD), pancreatic (PAAD), and gastric adenocarcinoma (STAD) were analyzed. We defined the pseudo-ischemic tumor ecosystem (PTES) as a transcriptomically defined molecular state reflecting coordinated malignant-cell stress and inflammatory-myeloid activity, rather than direct evidence of tissue ischemia or a diagnosis of cancer-associated thrombosis or venous thromboembolism. A tissue-resolved Core PTES, calculated as the mean of standardized malignant-stress and inflammatory-myeloid programs, was evaluated in 37 single-cell samples and 1107 TCGA tumors. Associations with immune states, Hallmark pathways, inferred cell-cell communication, and overall survival were assessed. The primary survival analysis used continuous Core PTES per one-standard-deviation increase, with high-versus-low PTES analyzed as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: Direct analysis showed the strongest effects for malignant stress (Hedges' g = 1.116), NET-like activity (g = 1.477), and endothelial activation (g = 1.288). Single-cell analysis retained 143,101 cells and localized malignant-stress and inflammatory-myeloid programs to their respective compartments. In TCGA, high Core PTES most strongly separated the inflammatory program (median difference = 1.134; rank-biserial r = 0.735). Cross-cancer GSEA identified recurrent proliferative, inflammatory, metabolic, and hypoxic programs, including E2F targets, G2M checkpoint, TNF-NF-κB, IL6-JAK-STAT3, glycolysis, and hypoxia. Inferred SPP1-CD44 and SPP1-ITGAV/ITGB1 interactions were detected across all three cancers. In multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, and stage, each one-standard-deviation increase in Core PTES was associated with poorer overall survival in LUAD (HR = 1.205, 95% CI 1.045-1.389) and PAAD (HR = 1.458, 95% CI 1.138-1.868), but not STAD (HR = 0.912, 95% CI 0.755-1.103); the cancer-stratified pooled HR was 1.168 (95% CI 1.060-1.288). High-versus-low sensitivity analyses showed the same cancer-specific pattern.

CONCLUSION: PTES captures a conserved pseudo-ischemic ecosystem linking malignant stress with inflammatory-myeloid remodeling. It is a hypothesis-generating, transcriptomically defined ecosystem measure rather than evidence of literal tissue ischemia, a diagnostic measure of cancer-associated thrombosis or venous thromboembolism, or a validated prognostic biomarker. Prospective clinical phenotyping and functional validation are required.

We investigated whether they define a conserved, transcriptomically measurable tumor state. title: Prevalence and associated factors of peripheral arterial disease in hemodialysis patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is common in hemodialysis patients and associated with adverse outcomes, but its prevalence and associated factors remain heterogeneous.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, CINAHL, CNKI, and Wanfang were searched from inception to April 8, 2026. Cross-sectional and cohort studies reporting PAD prevalence or associated factors were included. Random-effects models were used. Heterogeneity was explored using subgroup, meta-regression, and sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: The pooled prevalence was 23% (95%Confidence Intervals [CI], 20%∼26%) based on ankle brachial index ≤ 0.9, 42% (95%CI, 29%∼56%) based on ultrasonography or other imaging, and 19% (95%CI, 11%∼33%) based on clinical criteria. Both research regions and proportion of male were associated with heterogeneity. Factors associated with PAD included abdominal obesity (Odds Ratio [OR]=5.41), diabetes mellitus (OR=2.90), cardiovascular disease (OR=2.01), cerebrovascular disease (OR=1.91), male sex (OR=1.70), smoking (OR=1.64), hypertension (OR=1.34), C-reactive protein (OR=1.06), age (OR=1.04), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (OR=1.02), dialysis vintage (OR=1.01), albumin (OR=0.97), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (OR=0.94), Black race (OR=0.78), and serum creatinine (OR=0.75). Associations varied by diagnostic criteria.

CONCLUSIONS: PAD is common in hemodialysis patients, with prevalence varying substantially by diagnostic criteria and study settings. Several demographic and clinical characteristics were associated with PAD; however, most evidence was derived from cross-sectional studies and was of low or very low certainty. These findings should not be interpreted causally. Standardized diagnostic criteria and well-designed prospective studies are needed to improve the certainty and comparability of future evidence.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, CINAHL, CNKI, and Wanfang were searched from inception to April 8, 2026. title: Research Progressin Vitamins as Potential Nutritional Intervention Targets for Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a highly fatal vascular disease,yet effective pharmacological interventions to halt its progression are currently lacking.In recent years,vitamins have garnered significant attention as potential nutritional intervention targets due to their diverse physiological functions.This review systematically summarizes the research progress in the correlation between vitamins and AAA pathogenesis,and delves into the roles of vitamins in modulating key pathological processes such as inflammation,oxidative stress,matrix degradation,vascular smooth muscle cell function,and vascular calcification.Furthermore,this review analyzes the limitations of available studies and outlines future directions for nutritional interventions in AAA,with the ultimate goal of providing novel insights and scientific evidence for formulating the prevention and treatment strategies for AAA.

title: Research Evolution, Knowledge Structure, and Emerging Trends in Recurrent Venous Thromboembolism: A Bibliometric Analysis.
abstract: BackgroundRecurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) poses challenges for secondary prevention and long-term care. This study aimed to characterize the knowledge structure, research priorities, and thematic evolution of the recurrent VTE literature.MethodsA bibliometric analysis included 1,847 articles retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and PubMed Central. Python-based analyses examined country, institution, and author collaboration, citation patterns, keyword bursts, thematic clustering, and knowledge evolution.ResultsPublication output increased substantially, particularly after 2000, with the United States and Italy among the leading contributors. Major themes included thrombophilia, recurrence risk factors, anticoagulation, post-thrombotic syndrome, bleeding, cancer, and pulmonary embolism. Keyword bursts suggested an expansion from mechanistic research toward risk prediction, long-term outcomes, and individualized management.ConclusionsRecurrent VTE research has broadened toward risk assessment, treatment benefit-harm evaluation, and long-term outcomes. Further research should validate prediction tools across populations, establish the added value of biomarkers, and evaluate individualized secondary prevention.

title: Pharmacologic bridging to PTA in hyperkalemic hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVF: Impact on day surgery workflow and procedural feasibility.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hyperkalemia can delay percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) when dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) limit dialysis. We evaluated pharmacologic potassium lowering as a bridge to PTA on the day of presentation.

METHODS: We retrospectively screened 871 PTA encounters in a day surgery unit; 122 met potassium ⩾5.5 mmol/L. Six underwent emergency dialysis and 116 received pharmacologic bridge treatment. The primary endpoint was PTA on the day of presentation without rescue dialysis before PTA.

RESULTS: The primary endpoint occurred in 110/116 encounters (94.8%; 95% CI, 89.1%-98.1%). Paired potassium values were retrievable in 53 patients, decreasing from 6.14 ± 0.42 to 5.10 ± 0.65 mmol/L (p < 0.001). Technical, clinical, and immediate dialysis success were 100%, 98.1%, and 96.2%, respectively, in this detailed cohort. Numeric potassium after treatment was undocumented before the PTA decision in 57/116 encounters.

CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacologic bridging was feasible, but incomplete retrospective reassessment limits conclusions about safety and uniform biochemical reassessment.

title: Revascularisation Strategies in Dialysis-Dependent Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischaemia.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We reviewed dialysis-specific evidence on bypass and endovascular treatment for chronic limb-threatening ischaemia to assess how the available comparisons inform the initial revascularisation decision.

METHODS: We searched four bibliographic databases and one trial register through 12 September 2026. We synthesised comparisons without meta-analysis and graded certainty for eight outcomes. We applied nested restrictions by excluding mixed-open comparisons, retaining adjusted or matched comparisons, then excluding success-selected cohorts and abstract-only reports.

RESULTS: Sixteen reports represented 13 study families. Comparisons differed in whether they captured treatment attempted, treatment received or successful procedures. Selected comparisons reported associations favouring bypass for limb or wound outcomes. In the as-treated dialysis analysis of the Best Endovascular versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients with Critical Limb Ischaemia trial, single-segment great saphenous vein bypass was associated with lower reintervention hazard (hazard ratio 0.48, 95% confidence interval 0.25-0.94) and higher mortality (1.69, 1.06-2.70) than endovascular treatment. The estimate for amputation or death was imprecise (1.47, 0.95-2.27). Death handling for reintervention was unclear. Mixed-open comparisons suggested lower early amputation and more bleeding and wound complications. After successive restrictions, the remaining evidence did not establish an initial-strategy preference.

CONCLUSIONS: In dialysis-dependent CLTI, SSGSV bypass was associated with lower reintervention hazard but higher mortality in the as-treated BEST-CLI comparison; other favourable limb findings came from non-equivalent cohorts. These associations do not establish a net advantage or preferred initial strategy. Decisions should weigh limb threat, anatomy, conduit suitability, expected survival, perioperative risk, functional goals and treatment burden.

METHODS: We searched four bibliographic databases and one trial register through 12 September 2026. We synthesised comparisons without meta-analysis and graded certainty for eight outcomes.

title: Association between the stress hyperglycemia ratio and restenosis at 12 months after first percutaneous transluminal angioplasty in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether preoperative stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) is associated with 12-month target lesion restenosis after first percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) of autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) stenosis in patients on maintenance hemodialysis (MHD).

METHODS: We retrospectively included 158 MHD patients undergoing first PTA for autologous AVF stenosis at Shaoxing Second Hospital between January 2023 and December 2024. SHR was calculated from preoperative venous glucose and glycated hemoglobin A1c, and patients were grouped by quartiles. The primary endpoint was target lesion restenosis within 12 months, with all patients retained and follow-up administratively censored at 12 months. Cause-specific Cox models were fitted: Model 0 was unadjusted; Model 1 adjusted for age, sex, BMI, smoking, diabetes, hypertension, statin use and antiplatelet therapy; Model 2 further adjusted for dialysis vintage, access site, dialysis modality, pre-procedure stenosis severity, Ln(C-reactive protein), lesion length and vascular calcification. Kaplan-Meier analysis, restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses of 13 categorical factors, a Fine-Gray competing-risk model, exploratory mediation analysis and discrimination analysis were also performed.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 104 patients (65.8%) developed restenosis, 11 (7.0%) died before restenosis and 43 (27.2%) were censored at 12 months. Restenosis incidence from Q1 to Q4 was 25.6% (10/39), 50.0% (20/40), 94.9% (37/39) and 92.5% (37/40) (log-rank P < 0.001). Compared with Q1, fully adjusted Model 2 HRs for Q2-Q4 were 2.29 (95% CI 1.04-5.04; P = 0.039), 4.30 (2.08-8.87; P < 0.001) and 5.51 (2.52-12.07; P < 0.001). Each 1-SD increase in SHR was associated with an HR of 1.57 (1.25-1.96) in Model 2 (P < 0.001), and restricted cubic splines showed a nonlinear association (P < 0.001). Ln(CRP) was independently associated with restenosis (HR 1.62, 1.06-2.48; P = 0.027). Subgroup and competing-risk analyses were consistent; the exploratory indirect effect through Ln(CRP) was 0.090 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.000-0.199).

CONCLUSION: Preoperative SHR was independently associated with 12-month restenosis after first autologous AVF PTA in MHD patients, showing a nonlinear relationship. As it derives from routine laboratory tests, SHR may aid preoperative risk stratification; causality and clinical utility require prospective multicenter validation.

METHODS: We retrospectively included 158 MHD patients undergoing first PTA for autologous AVF stenosis at Shaoxing Second Hospital between January 2023 and December 2024. SHR was calculated from preoperative venous glucose and glycated hemoglobin A1c, and patients were grouped by quartiles.

title: The atherosclerotic cardiovascular-kidney-liver-metabolic burden in the Asia-Pacific, 1990-2050: A global burden of disease 2023 analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide, with the Asia-Pacific region bearing over half of this burden. The cardiovascular-kidney-liver-metabolic (CKLM) framework unifies the interrelated conditions of cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, which synergistically contribute to heightened cardiovascular risk. However, the combined CKLM burden in the region has not been characterised.

METHODS: Using the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023, we examined mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of CKLM diseases across 39 Asia-Pacific countries from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts to 2050. The CKLM burden was organized into metabolic antecedents (comprising CKD, MASLD, T2DM and obesity) and downstream atherosclerotic CVD (comprising ischemic heart disease, stroke, aortic aneurysm, and peripheral artery disease).

FINDINGS: In 2023, the Asia-Pacific recorded 286.9 million CKLM-related DALYs (53.2% of global burden), with an age-standardised DALY rate of 6390.9 per 100,000 population. From 1990 to 2023, crude DALYs rose by 78.7%, outpacing the global trends (61.1%), while age-standardised DALYs fell by 25.0% - driven by improvements in atherosclerotic CVD (-35.2%) but counterbalanced by a 20.4% rise in metabolic antecedents. By 2050, age-standardised DALY rates are projected to show a 7.0% point-estimate increase regionally against an estimated 14.9% global decline, with metabolic antecedents likely to expand from 29.9% to 36.2% of the total burden between 2026 and 2050. Intraregional disparities exist across sociodemographic strata, subregions, and age-sex categories. Risk-deleted analyses identify high systolic blood pressure, high fasting plasma glucose, and dietary risks as the highest-yield modifiable targets.

INTERPRETATION: The worsening Asia-Pacific CKLM trajectory is decoupling from improving global trends, driven by a compositional shift from atherosclerotic CVD toward upstream metabolic antecedents. Integrated interventions addressing multiple key modifiable risks are needed.

The cardiovascular-kidney-liver-metabolic (CKLM) framework unifies the interrelated conditions of cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, which synergistically contribute to heightened cardiovascular risk. However, the combined CKLM burden in the region has not been characterised.

title: Brain-computer interfaces for traumatic brain injury and spinal cord injury: Lesion-pattern matching, functional restoration, and clinical translation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are increasingly being developed for clinically relevant assessment, communication, rehabilitation, and functional restoration after central nervous system injury. However, their clinical roles differ substantially across injury types. This narrative review examines BCI applications in traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) using an injury-pattern-guided framework that links residual neural architecture with clinical tasks, interface selection, and outcome assessment.

MAIN BODY: In SCI, motor intention and cortical activity may remain accessible despite disruption of descending pathways, supporting motor-intention decoding, brain-controlled functional electrical stimulation, neuroprosthetic control, and brain-spine interfaces. In TBI, diffuse and heterogeneous network dysfunction shifts the clinical emphasis toward detection of covert consciousness, assisted communication, neurofeedback, and multimodal rehabilitation. We compare non-invasive, endovascular, electrocorticographic, and intracortical recording approaches; summarize evoked-response, motor-imagery, and continuous decoding paradigms; and distinguish functional substitution from closed-loop restoration of an individual's own movements. Recent invasive systems have supported the restoration of grasping, standing, and walking in selected individuals with SCI, whereas evidence in TBI remains concentrated on brain-state assessment and low-bandwidth communication.

CONCLUSION: Clinical translation will require careful candidate selection, stable long-term recordings, effective bidirectional feedback, clinically meaningful real-world outcomes, ethical oversight, and sustained technical support. Disease-specific translational pathways, rather than a universal BCI model, are likely to provide the most practical route to routine clinical use after central nervous system injury.

title: Repeated nasal and gingival bleeding caused by high-flow maxillary arteriovenous malformation: A case report.
abstract:
RATIONALE: Arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are congenital vascular anomalies characterized by abnormal direct connections between arteries and veins due to arrested embryonic development. Although rare, maxillary AVMs may lead to life-threatening hemorrhage. The association of epistaxis with maxillary AVMs has been relatively underemphasized in the literature.

PATIENT CONCERNS: We report the case of a 21-year-old female presenting with recurrent, profuse left-sided nasal and gingival bleeding.

DIAGNOSES: Clinical evaluation, computed tomography angiography, and digital subtraction angiography were performed for diagnosis.

INTERVENTIONS: Endovascular embolization was performed as the primary treatment, with staged embolization treatment and a total follow-up of 14 months.

OUTCOMES: A high-flow maxillary AVM was confirmed. The initial embolization successfully controlled the hemorrhage. At the 8-month follow-up after the initial embolization, residual lesions were detected and treated with a second embolization. At the 6-month follow-up after the second embolization, no recurrent bleeding was observed.

LESSONS: Maxillary AVMs may present with both gingival bleeding and epistaxis and can easily mimic common dental conditions. Early recognition and timely endovascular intervention are essential to prevent life-threatening hemorrhage.

Although rare, maxillary AVMs may lead to life-threatening hemorrhage. The association of epistaxis with maxillary AVMs has been relatively underemphasized in the literature.

title: Comparison of conventional logistic, random forest, and random forest-assisted models for 1-year primary patency after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula creation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We compared three strategies for predicting 1-year primary patency after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) creation.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 274 patients. Models A, B, and C were a 5-predictor logistic model, a 31-predictor random forest, and a 9-predictor random forest-assisted logistic model. The three models were compared in 251 patients with complete Model C predictors using 20 repeats of stratified 5-fold cross-validation.

RESULTS: Mean AUCs (SD) were 0.9361 (0.0045), 0.8843 (0.0095), and 0.9301 (0.0089) for Models A, B, and C; corresponding Brier scores were 0.0886 (0.0033), 0.1246 (0.0026), and 0.0933 (0.0060). Model A showed slightly better average cross-validated discrimination and prediction error than Model C, whereas Model C performed better than Model B.

CONCLUSIONS: Random forest-assisted modeling did not improve cross-validated predictive performance over the simpler logistic model. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 274 patients. Models A, B, and C were a 5-predictor logistic model, a 31-predictor random forest, and a 9-predictor random forest-assisted logistic model.

title: Pantothenate Metabolic Alterations in PROS1 Mutation Carriers and the Antithrombotic Effects of Pantethine.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients carrying PROS1 mutations are at increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, metabolic alterations linked to PROS1 mutations and their thrombotic contribution remain unclear.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to identify metabolic changes in PROS1-mutation patients through integrated multi-omics analyses, and to investigate the role of pantothenate derivatives in thrombosis using in vivo and in vitro models.

METHODS: Serum metabolomics, siRNA-mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE-2 cells, murine thrombosis models, and endothelial cell functional assays were employed.

RESULTS: Patients with PROS1 mutations exhibited significantly reduced serum levels of pantothenate derivatives, particularly pantetheine. siRNA-mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE-2 cells recapitulated this metabolic disturbance. In vivo, pantethine supplementation attenuated thrombus formation and platelet activation in murine models, accompanied by reduced serum levels of vWF and ICAM-1, and increased TFPI. In vitro, pantethine pretreatment suppressed NF-κB phosphorylation and reduced endothelial reactive oxygen species, counteracting IL-1β-induced procoagulant phenotype, leading to downregulation of vWF and ICAM-1 and upregulation of TFPI and THBD. Furthermore, pantethine-conditioned endothelial cells reduced responsiveness of co-incubated platelets, including attenuated spreading, aggregation, and activation. These findings associate PROS1 mutation-driven metabolic alterations with thrombotic risk, and suggest a metabolic-endothelial-platelet mode of interaction.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that patients with PROS1 mutations exhibit reduced circulating pantothenate derivatives, and that pantethine attenuates murine thrombosis and modulates endothelial and platelet function in vitro. These findings identify a metabolic-endothelial-platelet association in protein S deficiency. Whether PROS1 mutations directly cause pantothenate metabolic disturbance, and whether this disturbance mediates thrombosis, require testing in PROS1-deficient in vivo models.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Patients carrying PROS1 mutations are at increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, metabolic alterations linked to PROS1 mutations and their thrombotic contribution remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to identify metabolic changes in PROS1-mutation patients through integrated multi-omics analyses, and to investigate the role of pantothenate derivatives in thrombosis using in vivo and in vitro models.

title: Outcomes of Endovascular Repair for Stanford Type B Aortic Dissection with Concurrent Retrograde Intramural Hematoma Involving the Aortic Arch and/or Ascending Aorta (Zone 0-2) in a Chinese Population: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the outcomes of thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for type B aortic dissection (TBAD) with concurrent retrograde intramural hematoma (RTIMH) involving the aortic arch, with or without further extension into the ascending aorta.

METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE and EMBASE to June 2026 was performed. Studies reporting TEVAR outcomes in adults with TBAD-associated RTIMH, defined as a primary intimal tear at or distal to Ishimaru zone 3 with retrograde intramural hematoma extension into zones 0-2, were included. Co-primary outcomes were technical success and post-TEVAR retrograde type A aortic dissection (RTAD), defined as the new development of a communicating dissection flap within the previously non-flow intramural hematoma. Secondary outcomes included early mortality, stroke, type I endoleak, reintervention, survival, aortic rupture, and aortic remodelling. Proportions were pooled using single-arm random-effects meta-analysis following logit transformation; remaining findings were synthesised narratively.

RESULTS: Seven retrospective cohort studies comprising 342 patients, all from mainland Chinese institutions, were included. The pooled technical success rate was 99% (95% CI 97-99%; I2 = 0.0%). The pooled post-TEVAR RTAD rate was 3% (95% CI 1-8%; I2 = 7.6%), with all events preceded by proximal stent-graft-induced new entry. Secondary outcomes included pooled 30-day mortality of 2% (95% CI 1-4%; I2 = 0.0%), aortic rupture of 2% (95% CI 1-4%; I2 = 0.0%), reintervention of 7% (95% CI 5-11%; I2 = 0.0%), late all-cause mortality of 4% (95% CI 3-6%; I2 = 0.0%), and type I endoleak of 4% (95% CI 2-7%; I2 = 0.0%). All studies reporting pre- and post-procedural imaging demonstrated reductions in ascending aortic diameter and hematoma thickness, with complete ascending IMH resolution in 52.5-100% of patients.

CONCLUSIONS: TEVAR is technically feasible with low perioperative mortality and consistent aortic remodelling in selected patients with TBAD-associated RTIMH. Post-TEVAR RTAD and type I endoleak represent the principal procedure-specific risks. Contemporary evidence remains limited to small retrospective cohorts from a single geographic region.

Studies reporting TEVAR outcomes in adults with TBAD-associated RTIMH, defined as a primary intimal tear at or distal to Ishimaru zone 3 with retrograde intramural hematoma extension into zones 0-2, were included.

title: Risk factors for venous thromboembolism in adults with sepsis: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Adults with sepsis are at increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), encompassing deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), because of sepsis-related inflammation, endothelial injury, coagulation activation and treatment-related exposures. Although several potential risk factors have been reported, the evidence remains fragmented and findings are inconsistent across populations, VTE subtypes and diagnostic approaches. This protocol aims to prespecify transparent and reproducible methods for a systematic review and meta-analysis of factors associated with incident VTE in adults with sepsis.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: Prospective and retrospective cohort studies and case-control studies involving adults with sepsis or septic shock will be included. Studies evaluating potential risk factors for incident VTE after sepsis onset or diagnosis will be eligible. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, CINAHL and the Cochrane Library will be searched from inception to the final search date, supplemented by grey-literature searching and citation screening. Two reviewers will independently perform study selection, data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment. Where sufficient comparable data are available, random-effects meta-analysis will be conducted, with adjusted estimates prioritised. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses will be performed to explore heterogeneity, and certainty of evidence will be assessed using the GRADE approach adapted for prognostic-factor evidence.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420261465429.

title: A neonatal prediction model for lower-extremity peripherally inserted central catheters depth.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop a robust and generalizable prediction model for PICC depth in neonates undergoing lower-extremity catheterization, with the aim of improving the first-attempt success rate of catheter tip positioning and reducing PICC-related complications.

METHODS: A total of 240 neonates who successfully underwent lower-extremity PICC placement in the neonatal intensive care unit of a maternal and child health hospital were enrolled as study subjects. Variable selection was performed using stepwise regression based on the Akaike information criterion, followed by development of a multiple linear regression model. Internal validation was performed using the random split sample method (8:2). Model performance was assessed using root mean square error, mean absolute error, coefficient of determination (R2), and Pearson's correlation coefficient.

RESULTS: The final model included two simple and objective variables: body weight on the day of catheterization and puncture site. The prediction equation was established as follows: insertion depth (cm) = 17.3 + body weight at catheterization (kg) × 2.3 - adjustment value for the puncture site (2.7 for small saphenous vein, 4.5 for popliteal vein, 5.1 for popliteal great saphenous vein, and 10.3 for femoral vein, respectively; reference: ankle great saphenous vein). Internal validation showed that the model achieved an R2 of 0.8789, RMSE of 1.0754, MAE of 0.8157, and Pearson's correlation coefficient of 0.9375 between the predicted and observed values. Residual diagnostics indicated good predictive accuracy and stability.

CONCLUSIONS: The prediction model for neonatal lower extremity PICC insertion depth based on body weight at the catheterization and puncture sites demonstrated good fit and reliable predictive performance. It can assist in individualizing and precisely determining the catheter insertion depth in clinical practice, thereby reducing repeated adjustments and complications.

title: Limited arch repair versus extended arch repair for acute type A aortic dissection: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE(S): To compare early and long-term outcomes of limited arch repair versus extended arch repair for acute type A aortic dissection.

METHODS: Comparative studies evaluating limited (proximal) arch repair and extended arch repair were included. Studies with mixed isolated ascending or nonseparable proximal comparators were excluded from the primary synthesis. Random-effects meta-analyses using restricted maximum likelihood with Hartung-Knapp adjustment were performed to pool risk ratios for early binary outcomes and hazard ratios for long-term outcomes.

RESULTS: Twenty-five reports were included in the updated systematic review. After endpoint-specific adjudication of potentially overlapping institutional cohorts, the number of reports contributing to each pooled analysis varied by outcome. EAR was associated with a higher risk of early mortality (RR 1.31, 95% CI 1.01-1.70) and re-exploration for bleeding (RR 1.23, 95% CI 1.04-1.45). No statistically significant associations were detected for postoperative stroke (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.96-1.20) or dialysis (RR 1.21, 95% CI 0.99-1.49). HR-based analyses showed no statistically significant association with overall survival (HR 1.32, 95% CI 0.91-1.92) or distal aortic reintervention (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.07-13.78).

CONCLUSIONS: In retrospective observational comparisons, EAR was associated with higher early mortality and re-exploration for bleeding, whereas no statistically significant associations were detected for postoperative stroke or dialysis. No statistically significant associations were detected for overall survival or distal aortic reintervention. These findings do not establish causal effects of repair extent and remain limited by confounding by indication.

METHODS: Comparative studies evaluating limited (proximal) arch repair and extended arch repair were included. Studies with mixed isolated ascending or nonseparable proximal comparators were excluded from the primary synthesis.

title: A VAPG Incorporating Targeted Self-Assembling Peptides for Efficient VSMC Restoring and Imaging in Abdominal Aortic Models.
abstract: Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) dysfunction is closely associated with vascular remodeling during abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) progression, making VSMC repair a vital therapeutic strategy. Although peptides capable of VSMC recruitment have been reported, their application is severely limited by poor accumulation in AAA lesions because of rapid clearance following systemic administration. The enzyme-triggered self-assembling peptide strategy has emerged as a safe and effective approach to prolong local retention while enabling specific responsiveness. In this study, we identified ADAMTS4 and MMP-2 as highly expressed proteases in AAA lesions, serving as ideal targets for in situ retention. We developed a Targeted Responsive Assembly Peptide (TRAP) strategy by incorporating the VSMC-recruitment peptide VAPG, an ADAMTS4 recognition motif for AAA targeting, and an MMP-2-responsive cleavage motif that triggers self-assembly of the Fmoc-FF fragment. Following enzymatic activation, VAPG-containing fragments undergo self-assembly into hydrogels, significantly enhancing VSMC recruitment. The secondary structure transitioned from random coils to β-sheets upon MMP-2 cleavage. The assembled hydrogels exhibited moderate viscoelastic behavior, with stable elastic properties, favorable mechanical strength, and shear resistance. Moreover, PET/CT imaging revealed that 68Ga-labeled peptide enables non-invasive monitoring of peptide accumulation and retention at AAA sites. Ultimately, this TRAP strategy potentially serves as an efficient approach for AAA treatment through long-acting VSMC repair.

The enzyme-triggered self-assembling peptide strategy has emerged as a safe and effective approach to prolong local retention while enabling specific responsiveness.

title: Robot-assisted partial nephrectomy with venous tumor thrombectomy for classic renal angiomyolipoma: standardized technique and short-term outcomes.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To achieve the dual goals of effective tumor control and maximal renal function preservation, we have proposed a standardized robot-assisted nephron-sparing surgery combined with venous thrombectomy for classic renal angiomyolipoma (AML) with venous tumor thrombus (VTT). This study aimed to evaluate the technical feasibility and clinical rationality of this innovative surgical technique.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 17 patients who underwent robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) with venous tumor thrombectomy and 16 patients who underwent robot-assisted radical nephrectomy with venous tumor thrombectomy. The radical-nephrectomy cohort served as a historical clinical comparator. The modified thrombectomy strategy followed the proposed "NSS" technical principles. Functional and oncological outcomes were analyzed.

RESULTS: All procedures were completed without open conversion or intraoperative tumor-thrombus dislodgement, and no RAPN case required conversion to radical nephrectomy. The RAPN group had shorter operative time (160.0 vs. 232.5 min, p=0.021), shorter left renal vein clamping (3.0 vs. 16.5 min, p<0.001) and IVC clamping time (3.0 vs. 16.0 min, p<0.001), and better renal function preservation (p<0.001). Renal function was better preserved in RAPN group, primarily reflecting retention of the affected kidney. During the available follow-up (median 9 months in the RAPN group and 55 months in the Control group), no recurrence was detected; however, follow-up was insufficient for comparative or long-term oncological conclusions.

CONCLUSIONS: RAPN with venous tumor thrombectomy appears technically feasible in patients with classic renal AML with VTT. This surgical approach could better preserve renal function, but the long-term outcomes require confirmation in larger series with longer follow-up.

title: Pharmacological strategies for hemodialysis arteriovenous fistula and graft patency: an access-stratified systematic review and network meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pharmacological therapies target different stages of hemodialysis access failure. We compared treatments separately in arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) and grafts (AVGs), accounting for differences in outcomes and follow-up.

METHODS: This PROSPERO-registered review (CRD420261411441) followed PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-NMA guidance. PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL/Cochrane records, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through May 31, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed RoB 2. Separate random-effects frequentist network meta-analyses were supplemented by time-restricted analyses and exploratory follow-up meta-regression.

RESULTS: Among 1,557 records, 31 reports were included; 23 trial datasets contributed to the primary analyses (15 AVF and 8 AVG). In AVFs, ticlopidine (OR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.18-0.76) and clopidogrel (0.49; 0.24-0.97) may reduce predominantly early access failure (low certainty); estimates remained favorable at follow-up of 8 weeks or less. Larger single-trial effects for heparin plus anisodamine and clopidogrel plus a prostacyclin analog were very uncertain. Fish oil showed no clear AVF benefit. In AVGs, apixaban may reduce thrombosis (0.12; 0.03-0.41; low certainty), but its interval widened to 0.007-1.94 in the approximately 12-month subset. The aspirin estimate (3.35; 1.21-9.27) was very uncertain and imprecise under timing restrictions.

CONCLUSIONS: Ticlopidine and clopidogrel may reduce early AVF failure without established improvement in functional maturation. AVG apixaban findings require confirmation, and the effect of aspirin remains very uncertain. Interpretation depends on the clinical outcome, follow-up, and bleeding risk.

We compared treatments separately in arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) and grafts (AVGs), accounting for differences in outcomes and follow-up. METHODS: This PROSPERO-registered review (CRD420261411441) followed PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-NMA guidance.

title: Development and Internal Validation of an Integrated Clinical, Laboratory, and Ultrasound Model for 30-Day Venous Thromboembolic Deterioration After Acute Lower-Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis.
abstract: BackgroundShort-term prognostic tools for venous thromboembolic (VTE) deterioration after acute lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) are limited. We aimed to develop and internally validate a model integrating clinical, laboratory, and duplex ultrasound characteristics.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort included 785 adults with ultrasound-confirmed acute lower-extremity DVT from January 2018 to December 2025. The primary outcome was clinically detected and objectively confirmed ipsilateral DVT progression or new-onset symptomatic pulmonary embolism (PE) within 30 days. Three nested ridge-penalized logistic models included clinical predictors (Model 1), clinical plus laboratory predictors (Model 2), and clinical, laboratory, and ultrasound predictors (Model 3). Missing data were multiply imputed, and the complete modeling procedure was internally validated with 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Discrimination, calibration, Brier score, incremental performance, and decision-curve net benefit were assessed.ResultsThe primary outcome occurred in 102 patients (13.0%): 82 had DVT progression and 27 symptomatic PE, with seven having both. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.702, 0.766, and 0.808 (95% CI, 0.769-0.847) for Models 1-3, respectively. For Model 3, the optimism-corrected calibration slope was 0.94 and Brier score 0.087. Optimism-corrected ΔAUCs were 0.064 and 0.042, with corresponding ΔBrier scores of -0.009 and -0.008. Model 3 showed the highest optimism-corrected net benefit across thresholds of approximately 8%-25%. Observed outcome proportions across risk tertiles were 3.1%, 9.6%, and 26.3%.ConclusionsModel 3 provided internally validated prediction of clinically detected VTE deterioration under local treatment and imaging practices. External validation and prospective clinical-impact assessment are required before routine use.

title: A Two-Step Risk Stratification Model for Venous Thromboembolism Combining Caprini Score and D-Dimer in Trauma Patients Undergoing Surgery.
abstract: ObjectiveTo determine whether adding D-dimer to Caprini score-based risk assessment can further refine venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk stratification in trauma patients, particularly among those already classified as high-risk.MethodsA retrospective cohort of 206 trauma surgical patients who underwent surgical intervention was analyzed. Caprini scores and baseline plasma D-dimer levels were assessed against VTE occurrence using ROC curves. The two-step strategy consisted of initial Caprini-based stratification, followed by secondary D-dimer re-stratification using a study-derived exploratory threshold derived from the Youden index within the Caprini high-risk subgroup (Caprini score ≥9) in the same cohort. This threshold was not externally validated. All patients received mechanical VTE prophylaxis, while patients with Caprini scores ≥9 received prophylactic-dose low-molecular-weight heparin. Bilateral lower-extremity Doppler ultrasound was performed within 24 hours of admission, with subsequent surveillance according to predefined risk criteria.ResultsOverall composite VTE incidence was 31.1%. The Caprini score showed an AUC of 0.640 for VTE discrimination. D-dimer showed the highest discrimination in the full cohort (AUC = 0.669), which decreased to 0.614 within the Caprini high-risk subgroup (≥9 points, n = 118). Applying a study-derived exploratory D-dimer threshold of ≥5.5 mg/L identified a subgroup with a higher observed VTE incidence (44.8% vs. 16.1%; RR = 2.78, 95% CI: 1.21-6.37, P = 0.005). However, after adjustment for age, sex, and ISS, the association was attenuated and did not remain statistically significant (adjusted OR = 2.418, 95% CI: 0.660-8.864, P = 0.183).ConclusionsRelying solely on clinical risk scoring provides limited VTE discrimination in trauma patients. A sequential two-step strategy identified a subgroup with a higher observed VTE incidence within the Caprini high-risk category, although an independent association between the D-dimer threshold and VTE was not demonstrated after adjustment. This approach warrants prospective validation in larger cohorts.

Caprini scores and baseline plasma D-dimer levels were assessed against VTE occurrence using ROC curves. The two-step strategy consisted of initial Caprini-based stratification, followed by secondary D-dimer re-stratification using a study-derived exploratory threshold derived from the Youden index within the Caprini high-risk subgroup (Caprini score ≥9) in the same cohort.

title: Repurposing drugs for aortic aneurysm: unlocking new therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a life-threatening vascular disease for which no pharmacological therapy has been proven to effectively limit disease progression. Drug repurposing (DR), which leverages existing drugs with established safety profiles, offers a promising and cost-effective strategy to accelerate therapeutic development for AA. In this review, we summarize recent advances in DR research for AA, highlighting the emerging framework that integrates computational prediction with experimental and clinical validation. We discuss key repurposed drug candidates, evaluate the current state of translational evidence, and examine the challenges that have hindered clinical success despite encouraging preclinical findings. Finally, we outline opportunities to enhance target identification, patient stratification, and clinical trial design. By bridging mechanistic discovery and translational application, DR may provide a practical pathway toward effective medical therapies for aneurysmal disease.

Drug repurposing (DR), which leverages existing drugs with established safety profiles, offers a promising and cost-effective strategy to accelerate therapeutic development for AA. title: Endovascular robotic-assisted system for cerebral angiography (ERASE): Rationale, design, and protocol of a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Neurointerventional therapy is a cornerstone in managing head and neck vascular disorders, with cerebral angiography serving as its fundamental diagnostic and therapeutic backbone. However, manual cerebral angiography is associated with several inherent limitations. While existing robotic-assisted systems have shown promise in mitigating some of these issues, they face challenges such as limited compatibility, lengthy setup times, and a lack of high-quality real-world evidence. The ERASE trial is a multicenter, prospective, randomized controlled trial (RCT). A total of 660 eligible patients will be enrolled from seven comprehensive stroke centers in China and randomized 1:1 to either the robotic-assisted group or the control group. Both groups use the Seldinger technique for femoral/radial artery access. Operators undergo standardized training on the robotic system. The trial adopts a prospective randomized open-label blinded endpoint (PROBE) design, with all imaging endpoints adjudicated via blinded review by an independent imaging core laboratory. All patients are followed up at baseline, end of surgery, 24 h postoperatively, and 7 days post-discharge. The primary efficacy outcome is the clinical success rate. The primary safety outcome is the incidence of perioperative/postoperative complications (e.g., vascular perforation, dissection, pseudoaneurysm), serious adverse events, and device malfunctions. Secondary outcomes include technical failure rate, overall procedural time, pre-puncture setup time, mean catheterization time per target vessel, super-selective technique success rate, DSA fluoroscopy time, participant radiation dose, primary operator radiation dose, contrast agent volume and instrument performance evaluation. A key safety endpoint is the rate of new asymptomatic cerebral infarctions detected via postoperative brain MRI-diffusion-weighted imaging. As the RCT focusing on the YDHB-NS01 Ver 2.0 system, the ERASE trial addresses critical unmet needs in neurointerventional practice and will generate high-quality evidence for robotic-assisted cerebral angiography. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07182188. TRIAL REGISTRATION DATE: 2025-09-18.

title: [Effect of sequential multi-dose tranexamic acid administration on perioperative blood loss in cervical posterior single-door laminoplasty and its safety].
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effect of sequential multi-dose intravenous administration of tranexamic acid (TXA) on perioperative blood loss and inflammatory response in patients undergoing cervical posterior single-door laminoplasty (LMP), and to evaluate its safety.

METHODS: A prospective study was conducted in patients diagnosed with multi-level cervical spondylotic myelopathy, who underwent cervical posterior single-door LMP between January 2023 and June 2024. Using a computer-generated randomization table, patients were allocated into three groups. Placebo control group (group A): received 100 mL of normal saline intravenously at 30 minutes before incision (after anesthesia induction); the same dose was repeated every 5 hours for a total of 3 administrations. Single-dose control group (group B): received 1.0 g of TXA (dissolved in 100 mL normal saline) at 30 minutes before incision, followed by 100 mL of normal saline every 5 hours for a total of 2 additional doses. Sequential multi-dose group (group C): received 1.0 g of TXA (dissolved in 100 mL normal saline) at 30 minutes before incision, with an additional 1.0 g of TXA administered intravenously at 5 hours and 10 hours postoperatively, for a total dose of 3.0 g. A total of 120 patients met the selection criteria and were included in the study. After excluding lost-to-follow-up and withdrawn patients, 39 cases in group A, 37 in group B, and 38 in group C were included in the final analysis. There was no significant difference between groups (P>0.05) in age, gender, height, body weight, body mass index, comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes), and preoperative hematocrit (HCT), hemoglobin, D-dimer (D-D), interleukin 6 (IL-6), and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels. The primary outcome was total blood loss (TBL). Secondary outcomes included intraoperative blood loss (IBL), postoperative blood loss (PBL), drain removal time (DRT), HCT, D-D, IL-6, CRP, allogeneic blood transfusion rate, and incidence of complications.

RESULTS: Blood loss assessment: TBL, PBL, DRT, postoperative decline in HCT, and the allogeneic blood transfusion rate were all the lowest in group C, followed by group B, and the highest in group A, with significant differences between groups (P<0.05). The IBL was significantly lower in groups B and C than in group A (P<0.05), while there was no significant difference between groups B and C (P>0.05). Changes in inflammatory indicators: the levels of D-D and IL-6 in 3 groups reached peak at 1 day, the level of CRP reached peak at 3 days, and both decreased at 5 days, but still remained higher than preoperative levels, with significant differences (P<0.05). At different time points, the levels of D-D, IL-6, and CRP were significant lower in group C than in groups A and B (P<0.05), and in group B than in group A (P<0.05). Safety evaluation: During the 30-day postoperative follow-up, no deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, incisional infection, incisional hematoma, or TXA-related allergic reaction occurred in 3 groups.

CONCLUSION: Sequential multi-dose TXA administration effectively reduces perioperative blood loss in cervical posterior single-door LMP, suppresses postoperative hyperfibrinolysis and inflammatory response, shortens drainage duration, and does not increase the risk of thromboembolic events. This regimen represents a safe and effective optimization strategy for perioperative blood management in LMP.

METHODS: A prospective study was conducted in patients diagnosed with multi-level cervical spondylotic myelopathy, who underwent cervical posterior single-door LMP between January 2023 and June 2024. Using a computer-generated randomization table, patients were allocated into three groups.

title: Effect of Different Single-Session Durations of Intermittent Pneumatic Compression on the Prevention of Deep Vein Thrombosis in Postoperative ICU Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a common and potentially life-threatening complication in postoperative ICU patients. Intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) is widely used for mechanical thromboprophylaxis; however, the optimal single-session duration of IPC remains unclear. This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy of different single-session durations of IPC for preventing DVT in postoperative ICU patients. MATERIAL AND METHODS This prospective randomized controlled trial enrolled 138 patients who were randomized into 3 groups (n = 46 each) receiving IPC 3 times daily, with single-session durations of 40 minutes, 2 hours, or 6 hours. DVT incidence, coagulation parameters (D-dimer [mg/L] and fibrinogen [FIB; g/L]), and adverse events were compared on postoperative days 3 and 5. RESULTS Baseline characteristics were comparable among groups (P>0.05). The 6-hour group had a DVT incidence of 0% on both days, significantly lower than those in the 40-minute (15.21% and 32.61%) and 2-hour (8.70% and 34.78%) groups (P<0.05). No significant intergroup differences in D-dimer levels were observed (P>0.05); FIB levels significantly differed only on day 3 (P<0.05). Adverse events occurred in 6 patients (13.04%) in the 6-hour group, whereas none occurred in the other 2 groups. CONCLUSIONS Although 6-hour single-session IPC provides the most effective DVT prevention, it is associated with a higher risk of skin-related adverse events. Shorter, more frequent IPC (40 minutes or 2 hours per session, 3 times daily) may represent a preferable strategy for postoperative ICU patients due to its balance of efficacy, safety, and clinical feasibility.

This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy of different single-session durations of IPC for preventing DVT in postoperative ICU patients.

title: Comparison of Prosthetic Valve Deformation and Hemodynamic Performance Between Bicuspid and Tricuspid Aortic Valve Anatomy After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study compared prosthetic valve deformation and postprocedural hemodynamic performance between bicuspid and tricuspid aortic valve anatomy after transcatheter aortic valve replacement with the Venus-A prosthesis.

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated patients who underwent transcatheter aortic valve replacement between 2012 and 2022 and underwent postoperative computed tomography within 1 year. Predischarge echocardiographic assessments included the mean transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak. Computed tomography measurements included expansion ratio, ellipticity, implantation depth, asymmetric leaflet expansion, and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening. The leaflet inflow and valve waist were collectively defined as the functional valve portion.

RESULTS: Among 212 patients (106 bicuspid and 106 tricuspid), the mean age was 74.2±7.6 years, and 43.9% were women. Patients with bicuspid anatomy had a significantly lower oversizing ratio and underwent balloon predilation and postdilation more frequently than those with tricuspid anatomy. Residual transvalvular gradients were higher with bicuspid than tricuspid anatomy (12.0 [interquartile range, 8.2-17.0] versus 10.0 [7.2-14.0] mm Hg; P=0.014), whereas moderate to severe paravalvular leak did not differ significantly. Prosthetic ellipticity was greater in bicuspid anatomy, but expansion ratios, including those within the functional valve portion, did not differ significantly. Implantation depth, asymmetric leaflet expansion, and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening incidence also did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSIONS: Following Venus-A implantation, bicuspid anatomy was associated with greater prosthetic ellipticity and higher residual gradients, despite no significant difference in prosthetic expansion.

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated patients who underwent transcatheter aortic valve replacement between 2012 and 2022 and underwent postoperative computed tomography within 1 year. Predischarge echocardiographic assessments included the mean transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak.

title: Aortic valve disease associated inlet flow affects blood flow and nitric oxide transport: a potential role in ascending aortic dilation.
abstract: Aortic valve disease is associated with an increased risk of ascending aortic dilation and is characterized by abnormal inlet jet characteristics, which can regulate endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS)-mediated nitric oxide (NO) production through mechanobiological signaling. This study used computational fluid dynamics to quantify the effects of inlet jet tilt and axial rotation on aortic hemodynamics and NO response in a thoracic aortic model. Increasing inlet tilt shifted the jet toward the outer aortic wall, progressively altered helical flow from right-to left-handed, and increased time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS), transverse WSS (transWSS), and time-averaged WSS gradient (TAWSSG) while reducing oscillatory shear index (OSI) and relative residence time (RRT). Axial rotation primarily reorganized the spatial topology of helical flow and redistributed high-shear regions. Increasing inlet tilt elevated time-averaged NO (TANO) in the ascending aorta, with a marked increase along the right-anterior wall even at small tilt angles, whereas axial rotation increased TANO along the left wall. Notably, regions of increased TANO broadly corresponded to anatomical locations previously reported to be associated with ascending aortic aneurysm. These findings indicate that abnormal inlet jet characteristics can alter the aortic WSS and NO transport, suggesting a potential mechanobiological link to ascending aortic dilation.

title: Feasibility of patient-specific 3D-printed fragment models for preoperative planning in bicondylar tibial plateau fractures: a retrospective case series.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Schatzker type V and VI tibial plateau fractures have complex three-dimensional patterns that complicate surgical planning and coronal alignment restoration. This study assessed the feasibility of patient-specific 3D-printed fragment models for planning combined medial and lateral approaches and described radiographic and functional outcomes.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 22 patients with Schatzker type V or VI fractures treated at Foshan Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine from January 2023 to July 2024. Preoperative CT data enabled fragment segmentation, color coding, virtual reduction, and fabrication of patient-specific physical models. Posterior tibial slope, medial proximal tibial angle, articular depression, and tibial plateau width were compared pre- and postoperatively. Rasmussen functional and radiological scores and Knee Society Scores were assessed at 3 and 6 months, 1 year, and final follow-up; complications were recorded.

RESULTS: All 22 patients completed follow-up (mean, 30.73 ± 3.20 months). A mean of 24.41 ± 2.26 tibial fragments were identified and segmented per patient. Mean articular depression decreased from 6.70 ± 3.07 to 1.74 ± 0.48 mm. Posterior tibial slope, medial proximal tibial angle, and tibial plateau width improved significantly after surgery (all P < 0.001). Mean postoperative coronal alignment was within the predefined normal range in both preoperative varus and valgus subgroups. All three scores differed significantly across follow-up (all P < 0.001). At final follow-up, mean Rasmussen functional and Knee Society Scores were 27.18 ± 1.84 and 87.55 ± 4.92, respectively, with excellent-or-good rates of 100% and 95.45%. Mild post-traumatic knee osteoarthritis, superficial infection, and deep-vein thrombosis occurred in 5, 1, and 2 patients, respectively. No secondary varus or valgus deformity was observed.

CONCLUSIONS: In complex bicondylar tibial plateau fractures, patient-specific 3D-printed fragment models provided a practical three-dimensional reference for fragment identification, reduction sequencing, and planning of combined medial and lateral approaches. Satisfactory articular reduction, maintenance of proximal tibial coronal alignment, and favorable functional outcomes at final follow-up were observed in this cohort. These findings support the feasibility of incorporating 3D-printed fragment models into preoperative planning for these fractures.

This study assessed the feasibility of patient-specific 3D-printed fragment models for planning combined medial and lateral approaches and described radiographic and functional outcomes. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 22 patients with Schatzker type V or VI fractures treated at Foshan Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine from January 2023 to July 2024.

title: Association between nasogastric tube placement and self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms in patients receiving endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion: A post-hoc analysis of the ENCHANTED2/MT trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke anxiety and depression are common after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large vessel occlusion (LVO) and impair long-term recovery. Nasogastric tube (NGT) placement marks severe dysphagia and illness, but its association with anxiety or depression remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether NGT placement is associated with the presence and severity of 90-day self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms after successful EVT.

METHODS: We performed a post-hoc analysis of the ENCHANTED2/MT multicentre randomized controlled trial, including patients with anterior-circulation LVO who achieved successful reperfusion and had complete 90-day EQ-5D-3 L data. Participants were stratified by in-hospital NGT placement (No-NGT group vs. NGT group). The primary outcome was self-reported anxiety/depression assessed by the EQ-5D-3 L dimension (no, moderate, or extreme symptoms). We explored the association between NGT placement and the proportion and severity of self-reported anxiety/depression using propensity score matching (PSM) and logistic regression, and performed exploratory subgroup analyses.

RESULTS: Of 575 patients, 280(48.7%) received an NGT. Before matching, the proportion reporting self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms was 38.6% in the NGT group versus 15.6% in the no-NGT group (unadjusted OR3.40, 95%CI 2.30-5.09). After adjustment for measured clinical covariates, the association remained significant (adjusted OR2.97, 95%CI 1.93-4.63; ordinal OR3.06, 95%CI 1.99-4.77). After PSM, 175 patients were matched in each group; NGT placement remained associated with higher odds of self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms (37.7% vs 21.1%; OR2.26, 95%CI 1.41-3.65; ordinal OR2.25, 95%CI 1.41-3.63). In exploratory subgroup analyses, the association appeared more pronounced in patients with admission NIHSS ≤ 15 (OR3.83, 95% CI1.82-8.07; P for interaction = 0.049).

CONCLUSION: In this post-hoc analysis, NGT placement was associated with higher odds of self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms.NGT requirement may identify patients who deserve closer psychological assessment.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Post-stroke anxiety and depression are common after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large vessel occlusion (LVO) and impair long-term recovery. Nasogastric tube (NGT) placement marks severe dysphagia and illness, but its association with anxiety or depression remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether NGT placement is associated with the presence and severity of 90-day self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms after successful EVT.

title: Identification of the Nature of Acute Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion and Preferred Strategy for Mechanical Thrombectomy.
abstract: Acute middle cerebral artery occlusion is a common and critical cerebrovascular disease in clinical practice, characterized by its sudden onset and severe clinical symptoms, posing a substantial threat to neurological function and survival. Therefore, clinicians need to quickly and accurately identify the occlusion type and develop appropriate treatment plans accordingly. In recent years, with the development of neuroimaging technology and a deeper understanding of the pathophysiological mechanisms of acute middle cerebral artery occlusion, various diagnostic methods have been applied to determine the occlusion type. The core treatment goal of acute ischemic stroke is to minimize irreversible neuronal injury and restore effective brain tissue perfusion as soon as possible. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses of multiple randomized controlled trials have consistently confirmed that mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has significant clinical efficacy in acute anterior circulation stroke patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO). Therefore, domestic and international evidence-based guidelines list it as a first-line endovascular intervention for LVO stroke in the early stage of onset (within 6 h; expandable to 24 h with imaging screening). This narrative review summarizes current evidence on diagnostic approaches for different types of acute middle cerebral artery occlusion and mechanical thrombectomy strategies tailored to the presumed occlusion mechanism, with the aim of informing mechanism-based diagnostic assessment and endovascular treatment decisions.

title: Endovascular therapy for cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas: a single-center retrospective study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of endovascular therapy for cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas (CSDAVFs).

METHODS: A single-center, retrospective cohort study was conducted involving patients with CSDAVFs who underwent endovascular therapy performed by a single neurointerventionalist at West China Hospital, Sichuan University, between January 2023 and December 2025. Data collected included demographic characteristics, presenting symptoms and neurological signs, baseline and follow-up imaging findings (including digital subtraction angiography), procedural details (e.g., access route, embolic agents, technical success), and clinical outcomes-including angiographic occlusion status, symptom resolution, procedure-related complications, and functional recovery.

RESULTS: Fourteen patients were diagnosed with cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas (CSDAVFs). Twelve underwent endovascular treatment following definitive diagnosis by digital subtraction angiography (DSA); two declined intervention despite confirmed diagnosis. Thirteen presented with predominant ocular manifestations-such as proptosis, chemosis, and ophthalmoparesis-while one was diagnosed incidentally on cranial MRI performed for headache and dizziness. All 12 patients underwent the procedure successfully: seven underwent arterial-access embolization and five underwent venous-access embolization. Onyx liquid embolic agent was used as the sole embolic material in seven cases; in the remaining five cases, detachable coils were employed as adjunctive agents. Immediate post-procedural DSA demonstrated complete occlusion in nine patients and subtotal occlusion in three. Procedure-related complications occurred in five patients: visual acuity reduction (n = 2), ipsilateral facial hypoesthesia (n = 2), and isolated impairment of abduction and downward gaze (n = 1). Symptomatic improvement was observed in seven patients. At 1-year clinical and imaging follow-up, all 12 treated patients remained under surveillance. Ten exhibited no recurrence; notably, one patient with initial subtotal occlusion achieved complete angiographic occlusion during follow-up. In the remaining two, residual lesions remained stable in size, symptoms improved, and no secondary intervention was required. Among the five patients with procedure-related complications, two developed persistent facial hypoesthesia after intra-arterial embolization; subjective numbness gradually improved but did not fully resolve during follow-up.

CONCLUSION: Endovascular therapy for craniospinal dural arteriovenous fistula (CSDAVFs) is associated with favorable clinical and angiographic outcomes. Although procedure-related complications occur in a subset of patients, most are transient and resolve spontaneously or improve to partial remission during follow-up. Collectively, these findings support endovascular therapy as a safe and effective treatment modality for CSDAVFs.

METHODS: A single-center, retrospective cohort study was conducted involving patients with CSDAVFs who underwent endovascular therapy performed by a single neurointerventionalist at West China Hospital, Sichuan University, between January 2023 and December 2025.
