title: Association between the triglyceride-glucose index and clinical outcomes in acute atherosclerotic ischaemic stroke patients following endovascular thrombectomy: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to investigate the association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and unfavourable clinical outcomes in patients with atherosclerotic acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT).

METHODS: Patients with AIS who underwent EVT between January 2019 and September 2024 were enrolled. The primary outcome was an unfavourable functional outcome at three months (modified Rankin Scale score 3-6); secondary outcomes were symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage (sICH) and all-cause mortality at three months. The TyG index was analysed continuously and in quartiles by logistic regression, restricted cubic splines and receiver operating characteristic curves.

RESULTS: Among 670 patients, 269 (40.1%) had an unfavourable functional outcome at three months, 91 (13.6%) died at three months for all-cause, and 85 (12.7%) developed sICH. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest TyG quartile was independently associated with unfavourable functional outcome (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.91, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-3.56) and mortality (aOR 5.15, 95% CI 2.06-12.86). The overall spline association was significant for all endpoints; only mortality was non-linear (P = 0.032), with risk rising above a TyG index of approximately 8.9. Discrimination was modest, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.583 for unfavourable functional outcome and 0.612 for mortality. No significant interactions were found across prespecified subgroups, except for blood glucose level.

CONCLUSION: An elevated TyG index is independently associated with three-month unfavourable functional outcome, mortality and sICH after EVT, and may aid prognostic risk stratification, although further validation is required based on the existing predictive indicators.

METHODS: Patients with AIS who underwent EVT between January 2019 and September 2024 were enrolled. The primary outcome was an unfavourable functional outcome at three months (modified Rankin Scale score 3-6); secondary outcomes were symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage (sICH) and all-cause mortality at three months.

title: Noninvasive electrical impedance tomography monitoring during total aortic arch replacement: incremental value for prediction of postoperative neurological deficit.
abstract: Introduction: Postoperative neurological deficit (ND) after total aortic arch replacement (TAAR) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, with limited effective preventive therapies available. Intraoperative neuromonitoring plays a critical role in reducing postoperative ND. This prospective cohort study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of electrical impedance tomography (EIT) and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) for predicting postoperative ND in patients undergoing TAAR. Methods: A 16-electrode EIT system and NIRS were utilized for intraoperative cerebral neuromonitoring during TAAR. Correlations between intraoperative EIT and NIRS variables and postoperative ND were comprehensively analyzed. Results: The overall incidence of postoperative ND was 39.1% (59/151), including a 15.2% incidence of postoperative stroke. The time integral of absolute resistivity asymmetry index during hypothermic circulatory arrest (TRAIHCA), the maximum absolute resistivity asymmetry ratio during HCA (MRARHCA), age, body mass index, supra-aortic branch involvement, and operative duration were independent predictors of postoperative ND. Incorporation of EIT parameters into the clinical prediction model significantly improved the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve from 0.752 to 0.817 (P = 0.027). Moreover, the incremental prognostic value of EIT was further validated by improved risk reclassification and discriminatory ability for ND, with a net reclassification index of 0.510 (P = 0.002) and an integrated discrimination improvement of 0.072 (P < 0.001). Conclusion: The EIT parameters have been demonstrated to be an effective means of predicting ND following TAAR. Cerebral EIT may represent a potential alternative for intraoperative noninvasive multimodal neuromonitoring options.

Intraoperative neuromonitoring plays a critical role in reducing postoperative ND. This prospective cohort study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of electrical impedance tomography (EIT) and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) for predicting postoperative ND in patients undergoing TAAR.

title: Intraoperative measurement of the ascending aortic diameter at the onset of aortic dissection.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although prior studies have associated aortic size with dissection risk, none have corrected for dissection-related aortic expansion. This study aimed to establish a measurement approach to determine the ascending aortic diameter before dissection.

METHODS: The samples of dissected ascending aortas were obtained from 36 patients at the time of their operation. In this study, the intimal lumen diameter measured at its maximal stretching state was used as a reliable surrogate for the pre-dissection aortic diameter. Subsequently, the relationship between this surrogate and the aortic diameter measured on post-dissection CT at the corresponding levels was further analyzed.

RESULTS: Using this method, the pre-dissection ascending aortic diameter was measured as 37.5 ± 6.6 mm, whereas the post-dissection CT measurement at the same level increased to 43.9 ± 7.0 mm. After excluding patients with non-A-non-B aortic dissection, the mean ascending aortic diameter increased by approximately 20% after dissection compared with the pre-dissection value, corresponding to an absolute increase of 7.5 mm in diameter.

CONCLUSIONS: Although aortic diameter remains a robust indicator for prophylactic surgery in the study population, acute aortic dissection is seldom associated with true ascending aortic aneurysms and occurs with normal or near-normal aortic dimensions in most patients. When dissection occurs in the setting of a small aortic diameter, it likely reflects a profound functional vulnerability of the aortic tissue to catastrophic aortic events.

This study aimed to establish a measurement approach to determine the ascending aortic diameter before dissection. METHODS: The samples of dissected ascending aortas were obtained from 36 patients at the time of their operation.

title: Case Report: Splenorenal shunt management after liver transplantation in a recipient with situs inversus totalis.
abstract: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) alters graft positioning and vascular reconstruction during liver transplantation. A 56-year-old man with SIT, decompensated hepatitis B cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma received a 558-g deceased-donor whole-liver graft, with a graft-to-recipient weight ratio of 0.60%. The graft was implanted in the native left-sided hepatic fossa in a reversed orientation. Postoperative CT showed a large splenorenal shunt and heterogeneous graft enhancement. Portal vein velocity fell from 44.7 cm/s on postoperative day (POD) 1 to 25 cm/s on POD3-4 and was 32 cm/s on POD5. Endovascular occlusion was abandoned on POD5 because venography showed aneurysmal dilatation and the procedural risk was judged excessive. Open ligation of the approximately 3-cm shunt was performed on POD6, preserving the main renal vein. Portal vein velocity was 30 cm/s after ligation, 37 cm/s on POD7 and 42 cm/s on POD9. Total bilirubin decreased from 158.6 μmol/L on POD4 to 70.5 μmol/L on POD13; the international normalized ratio was 1.49 on POD6 and 1.02 on POD14. The patient was discharged on POD27. Imaging showed no tumor recurrence at approximately 19 months, and alpha-fetoprotein was 7.32 ng/mL at approximately 23 months. This case describes surgical treatment of suspected portal steal in an SIT recipient when endovascular shunt occlusion was unsuitable.

A 56-year-old man with SIT, decompensated hepatitis B cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma received a 558-g deceased-donor whole-liver graft, with a graft-to-recipient weight ratio of 0.60%. The graft was implanted in the native left-sided hepatic fossa in a reversed orientation.

title: Oral anticoagulants and the risk of acute kidney injury: a retrospective real-world cohort study using overlap propensity score weighting.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anticoagulant-related nephropathy, initially described in association with warfarin, has increasingly been reported with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs). However, the comparative risk of acute kidney injury (AKI) within 30 days of treatment initiation between warfarin and DOACs across a broad spectrum of clinical indications remains unclear.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients newly initiated on DOACs or warfarin between January 2014 and May 2025 at the Third Xiangya Hospital of Central South University. Overlap propensity score weighting, with weights derived from a generalized boosted model incorporating 81 baseline covariates, balanced the treatment groups. Weighted logistic regression compared the risk of AKI within 30 days of OAC initiation, defined by KDIGO criteria. Sensitivity analyses included inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and logistic regression-derived overlap weighting, each with or without doubly robust covariate adjustment.

RESULTS: Among 6 876 patients (5 048 DOAC users; 1 828 warfarin users), DOAC initiation was associated with a higher risk of AKI than warfarin after overlap weighting (OR: 1.346, 95% CI: 1.057-1.715; p = 0.016), and with severe AKI (stage 2-3; OR: 1.694, 95% CI: 1.013-2.832; p = 0.044), whereas stage 1 AKI did not differ significantly. The association persisted after additional covariate adjustment (OR: 1.363, 95% CI: 1.068-1.740; p = 0.013) and across alternative propensity score models, although the unadjusted IPTW model did not. By indication, the association was significant for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF) (OR: 1.566, 95% CI: 1.034-2.369; p = 0.034) but not for venous thromboembolism (VTE) treatment or prophylaxis. Among individual DOACs, rivaroxaban was associated with an elevated risk (OR: 1.392, 95% CI: 1.075-1.804; p = 0.012), whereas edoxaban, dabigatran, and apixaban were not. Lower-dose rivaroxaban initiation was associated with an increased risk (OR: 2.792, 95% CI: 1.524-5.114; p = 0.001), whereas higher-dose and off-label use were not. In prespecified subgroup analyses, ORs were above 1 in most strata, but most comparisons were not significant, and no significant interactions were detected.

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that DOACs, particularly rivaroxaban, may be associated with a higher short-term risk of AKI than warfarin. Given the expanding use of DOACs, medication-specific renal effects warrant further investigation, and close monitoring of renal function may be advisable in high-risk patients after anticoagulation initiation.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Anticoagulant-related nephropathy, initially described in association with warfarin, has increasingly been reported with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs). However, the comparative risk of acute kidney injury (AKI) within 30 days of treatment initiation between warfarin and DOACs across a broad spectrum of clinical indications remains unclear. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients newly initiated on DOACs or warfarin between January 2014 and May 2025 at the Third Xiangya Hospital of Central South University.

title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analysis identifies a PLAUR-centered macrophage-associated programmed cell death signature in type A aortic dissection.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type A aortic dissection (TAAD) is a life-threatening aortic emergency characterized by inflammatory remodeling, extracellular matrix disruption, and programmed cell death (PCD). The cell-specific transcriptional features associated with immune activation and PCD-related aortic wall injury remain incompletely defined. This study investigated PCD-associated immune remodeling in TAAD and evaluated PLAUR as a macrophage-associated marker linked to these pathological changes.

METHODS: Public bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated with single-cell RNA sequencing, curated PCD-related gene sets, immune deconvolution, pathway enrichment, in silico perturbation analysis, and histological assessment of human aortic specimens.

RESULTS: TAAD tissues exhibited marked transcriptomic alterations, with 2,217 genes meeting the exploratory differential-expression criteria, accompanied by increased PCD-related transcriptional activity. Single-cell analysis indicated that macrophage-enriched clusters showed relatively high PCD-related gene-set activity, while PLAUR transcripts were predominantly detected in macrophage-enriched clusters. PLAUR was upregulated in TAAD in both training and external validation datasets and strongly correlated with sample-level PCD scores. In the training dataset, PLAUR expression showed exploratory discrimination between TAAD and control tissue samples, with an AUC of 0.858. PLAUR-high samples showed enrichment of HIF-1, JAK-STAT, necroptosis, and apoptosis-related pathways. Immune deconvolution indicated relatively higher neutrophil- and M0 macrophage-associated signatures in TAAD, with PLAUR expression positively associated with myeloid-cell-related features. In silico perturbation analysis identified cytoskeletal and actin-related transcriptional changes associated with predicted PLAUR perturbation. Histological assessment demonstrated aortic wall disorganization, collagen remodeling, elastic fiber disruption, increased TUNEL positivity, and elevated PLAUR protein expression in TAAD lesions.

CONCLUSIONS: PLAUR is associated with macrophage-enriched inflammatory, proteolytic, and PCD-related remodeling in TAAD and may serve as a candidate marker of these pathological features. The present findings are associative and do not establish a causal role for PLAUR in aortic wall degeneration or dissection initiation. Spatially resolved and functional studies are required to determine whether PLAUR-positive macrophage states contribute mechanistically to TAAD pathogenesis.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Type A aortic dissection (TAAD) is a life-threatening aortic emergency characterized by inflammatory remodeling, extracellular matrix disruption, and programmed cell death (PCD). The cell-specific transcriptional features associated with immune activation and PCD-related aortic wall injury remain incompletely defined. This study investigated PCD-associated immune remodeling in TAAD and evaluated PLAUR as a macrophage-associated marker linked to these pathological changes.

title: Application of endovascular stent graft in ABO-incompatible living donor kidney transplantation: a case report.
abstract: Severe iliac arteriosclerosis is a contraindication for kidney transplantation (KT). This report details a case of a 34-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus and severe iliac arteriosclerosis who underwent ABO-incompatible living donor KT in which the renal graft artery was anastomosed to the self-expandable endovascular covered stent placed in the external iliac artery. The initial anti-blood group anti-A antibody titers were 1:4 and 1:32 for IgG and IgM, respectively. Routine pre-transplant therapy including rituximab 200mg, triple immunosuppressants included tacrolimus (7mg/d, tacrolimus concentration was between 3.8 and 9.2 ng/mL), mycophenolate mofetil (1500mg/d), methylprednisolone (16mg/d). Following one session of double filtration plasmapheresis, anti-blood group antibody titers were reduced 1:4 and 1:8 for IgG and IgM. Two days prior to surgery, patient underwent one session of plasma exchange and antibody titers were IgG 1:4 and IgM 1:8 on the day of KT. Basiliximab was administered for immune induction. The initial routine was performed with conventional end-to-side anastomosis between the renal graft artery and the right external iliac artery. However, pulsation of the transplant renal artery disappeared shortly. Upon opening the anastomosis, thrombosis at the anastomotic site was identified due to plaque embolism from the external iliac artery. Consequently, a self-expandable endovascular covered stent was implanted into the external iliac artery via the right femoral artery under intervention. Because part of the external iliac artery wall was defective, the endovascular stent was partially exposed, used the prosthetic graft for coverage and reinforcement. Finally, the renal allograft artery was anastomosed end-to-side to the stent-prosthetic complex. The anti-blood group antibody titers were 1:2 and 1:4 for IgG and IgM and serum creatinine was 124 μmol/L at 1 month. During the 2 years follow-up, graft function remained satisfactory, the serum creatinine levels were 116, 107, and 113 μmol/L at 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years postoperatively, and no signs of right lower limb ischemia were evident. This study demonstrates that renal graft implanted on the endovascular stent is a feasible therapeutic option for recipients with severe iliac arteriosclerosis.

This report details a case of a 34-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus and severe iliac arteriosclerosis who underwent ABO-incompatible living donor KT in which the renal graft artery was anastomosed to the self-expandable endovascular covered stent placed in the external iliac artery. The initial anti-blood group anti-A antibody titers were 1:4 and 1:32 for IgG and IgM, respectively.

title: Genetic-multi-omics causal inference coupled with integrative in-vitro toxicology reveals immune-metabolite mediators for aortic aneurysm risk.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a life-threatening vascular disease characterized by immune disturbance and metabolic dysregulation. Multi-omics-driven precision toxicity prediction, integrating human genetic causal inference with functional in-vitro toxicology, remains under-explored for uncovering metabolite mediators underlying AA disease risk.This study aimed to dissect metabolite-dependent causal pathways linking immune cells to AA, and evaluate dose-response cytotoxicity of key mediating metabolites toward vascular cells.

METHODS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and two-step mediation analysis were performed using European-ancestry GWAS summary datasets covering 731 immune-cell traits, 1,091 plasma metabolites, 3,230 AA cases and 475,964 controls. Complementary in-vitro CCK-8 cytotoxicity experiments on human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs) were further conducted for candidate metabolites Adrenate (22:4n6) and BAFF-R.

RESULTS: BAFF-R on CD20- (OR = 0.859, 95%CI: 0.797-0.926, P = 7.17 × 10-5) and, to a lesser extent, Granulocyte AC (OR = 0.900, 95%CI: 0.843-0.961, P = 1.57 × 10-3) emerged as candidate protective immune-cell markers for AA. Adrenate (22:4n6) and Nisinate (24:6n3) mediated 4.47% and 9.84% of these protective effects, respectively. Adrenate triggered significant dose-dependent cytotoxicity in HASMCs.

CONCLUSION: This multi-omics genetic-toxicology study provides causal genetic evidence for immune-metabolite regulatory axes in AA pathogenesis. Notably, Adrenate presents dual biological effects: it transmits immune-protective signals but exerts direct vascular cellular toxicity. Our findings highlight the utility of MR-assisted precision toxicity prediction for disease risk evaluation and therapeutic target mining for AA.

METHODS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and two-step mediation analysis were performed using European-ancestry GWAS summary datasets covering 731 immune-cell traits, 1,091 plasma metabolites, 3,230 AA cases and 475,964 controls.

title: Hemodynamic changes after artificial vessel reconstruction for common iliac artery aneurysm: a case report.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Isolated iliac artery aneurysms (IIAA) frequently coexist with abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA), yet their causal association remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate hemodynamic alterations following artificial vessel reconstruction for iliac aneurysm and its impact on the abdominal aorta and iliac artery.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 54-year-old man with a history of thyroid adenoma presented with left lower abdominal pain. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) revealed an aneurysm involving the entire left common iliac artery (48 mm × 55 mm × 81 mm). The patient was hemodynamically stable, with unremarkable physical examination and laboratory findings. He underwent aneurysm resection and aortoiliac reconstruction with a synthetic graft. Intraoperatively, arterial tortuosity and marked dilation at the bifurcation were noted. Postoperative CTA confirmed graft patency, and the patient recovered uneventfully. Preoperative and postoperative CTA scans were used for three-dimensional vascular reconstruction, followed by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to assess hemodynamic parameters including wall shear stress (WSS), blood pressure, and flow velocity.

CONCLUSION: Prosthetic vascular reconstruction for common iliac artery aneurysm (CIAA) may produce dual hemodynamic effects on the abdominal aorta. While the causal link between CIAA and AAA is unproven, the surgery eliminates rupture risk of the target aneurysm. These exploratory results may provide hemodynamic references to optimize surgical planning for iliac artery aneurysms.

This study aimed to investigate hemodynamic alterations following artificial vessel reconstruction for iliac aneurysm and its impact on the abdominal aorta and iliac artery. CASE PRESENTATION: A 54-year-old man with a history of thyroid adenoma presented with left lower abdominal pain.

title: Social-biological misalignment modulates the prognostic impact of infarct volume after endovascular thrombectomy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) achieves high rates of reperfusion, yet functional recovery remains heterogeneous. We investigated whether social-biological time misalignment modifies the association between final infarct volume and 90-day functional outcome.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 160 patients with large vessel occlusion treated with EVT. Misalignment was quantified using a composite score incorporating occupational shift exposure and symptom onset timing. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the interaction between misalignment and final infarct volume on favorable 90-day outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0-2).

RESULTS: Misalignment was not independently associated with favorable outcome. However, a significant interaction was observed (OR = 9.70, 95% CI 1.74-54.10, LRT p = 0.008), remaining significant after FDR correction (q = 0.034), stable across profile likelihood and Firth penalized regression. The interaction improved model fit (AIC 124.35 → 119.38) and provided modest incremental net benefit. Exploratory threshold analysis suggested a potential inflection point approximating 25 mL, but this is hypothesis-generating and requires validation.

CONCLUSION: Misalignment does not exert a uniform adverse effect but acts as a state-dependent modifier, modifying the association between final infarct volume and favorable outcome. The interaction between chronobiological state and infarct burden offers a novel framework for understanding outcome heterogeneity.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) achieves high rates of reperfusion, yet functional recovery remains heterogeneous. We investigated whether social-biological time misalignment modifies the association between final infarct volume and 90-day functional outcome. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 160 patients with large vessel occlusion treated with EVT.

title: Machine-learning-derived laboratory signatures associated with postoperative day-3 ultrasound-detected lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis after fractures around the knee.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to construct risk-discrimination models for postoperative-day-3 ultrasound-detected lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) status in patients with fractures around the knee (FAK) using five machine-learning algorithms and compare model performance across five machine-learning algorithms.

METHODS: Electronic medical records of 1,071 patients who underwent surgical treatment for FAK at Suining Central Hospital from January 2023 to August 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 749) and a test set (n = 322) at a 7:3 ratio. Feature selection occurred exclusively within the training dataset. Predictive variables were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, the Boruta algorithm, and recursive feature elimination-extreme gradient boosting (RFE-XGBoost). Five predictive models were developed, including logistic regression, k-nearest neighbor (KNN), random forest (RF), light gradient-boosting machine (LightGBM), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). Model performance was evaluated comprehensively via the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score. Receiver-operating-characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision-curve analysis (DCA) were utilized to identify the selected model. Finally, Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were employed to interpret the global and local prediction outputs of the selected model.

RESULTS: Seventeen overlapping features were identified via feature-selection procedures for final modelling, among which postoperative-day-1 and postoperative-day-3 laboratory biomarkers contributed most substantially to model output. XGBoost was chosen for subsequent SHAP interpretability analyses based on balanced performance observed in cross-validated out-of-fold outputs from the training set. Several non-linear models yielded comparably high discrimination, with overlapping 95% confidence intervals for AUROC.The cross-validated AUC for the XGBoost model in the training set was 0.9932, with a classification threshold of 0.57 derived from the Youden index. In the test set, the AUROC was 0.998 (95% CI: 0.993-1.000), AUPRC was 0.996 (95% CI: 0.988-1.000), accuracy was 0.991 (95% CI: 0.978-1.000), sensitivity was 0.969 (95% CI: 0.930-1.000), specificity was 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000), precision was 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000), and F1-score was 0.984 (95% CI: 0.964-1.000). The Brier score for the test set was 0.013. Calibration curves and decision-curve analysis demonstrated favourable probability calibration and higher estimated net benefit across a range of threshold probabilities. SHAP-value analysis highlighted that postoperative-day-1 CRP, postoperative-day-3 FIB, postoperative-day-3 APTT, postoperative-day-3 CRP, postoperative-day-3 FDP, postoperative-day-3 PT, postoperative-day-1 UREA, and postoperative-day-1 CREA were major contributing features.

CONCLUSION: The XGBoost model demonstrated excellent discrimination and favorable calibration in the internal test set for identifying postoperative-day-3 ultrasound-detected DVT among patients with FAK. However, several predictors in the final model were measured on postoperative day 3, temporally proximate to the time-point of DVT ascertainment; these biomarkers may reflect biochemical changes secondary to already-formed thrombus rather than pre-thrombotic prospective risk signals. Therefore, the near-perfect discrimination observed in this retrospective cohort should be interpreted cautiously and should not be regarded as definitive evidence of prospective early-prediction performance. Temporal and multicenter external validation using a prespecified prediction time point, ideally restricted to variables available prior to DVT assessment, is required to determine the model's generalizability and prospective clinical applicability.

METHODS: Electronic medical records of 1,071 patients who underwent surgical treatment for FAK at Suining Central Hospital from January 2023 to August 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 749) and a test set (n = 322) at a 7:3 ratio.

title: Triglyceride-glucose index and the incidence of peripheral artery disease: a dose-response meta-analysis of longitudinal studies.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a simple surrogate marker of insulin resistance and has been increasingly investigated as a predictor of cardiovascular diseases. However, longitudinal evidence regarding its association with incident peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains limited and inconsistent. We conducted a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis to evaluate the association between the TyG index and the risk of incident PAD.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were systematically searched from inception to June 28, 2026. Longitudinal observational studies evaluating the association between the conventional TyG index and incidents PAD in adults were eligible. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) comparing the highest versus lowest TyG categories were calculated using restricted maximum likelihood random-effects models. Linear and nonlinear dose-response meta-analyses were performed using restricted cubic spline models.

RESULTS: Five longitudinal studies involving 417,499 participants and 7,800 incident PAD events were included. Compared with the lowest TyG category, a high TyG index was associated with a significantly increased risk of incident PAD (RR = 1.49, 95% CI 1.06 to 2.10; p = 0.02), although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 88.4%). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated robust findings. In the linear dose-response meta-analysis, each 1-unit increase in the TyG index was associated with a 22% higher risk of incident PAD (RR = 1.22, 95% CI 1.08 to 1.37; p = 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a significant overall dose-response association (p = 0.001) with no evidence of nonlinearity (p for nonlinearity = 0.367), indicating an approximately linear relationship between the TyG index and PAD risk.

CONCLUSIONS: A higher TyG index is associated with an increased risk of incident PAD in a dose-dependent and approximately linear manner.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261470450.

However, longitudinal evidence regarding its association with incident peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains limited and inconsistent. We conducted a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis to evaluate the association between the TyG index and the risk of incident PAD.

title: Efficacy and safety of flow diverters for middle cerebral artery bifurcation aneurysms: a retrospective dual-center study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of flow diverters (FDs) for the treatment of middle cerebral artery (MCA) bifurcation aneurysms.

METHODS: This retrospective, dual-center study enrolled 29 patients with unruptured MCA bifurcation aneurysms treated with flow diverters (FDs) between January 2021 and December 2024. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS), where scores of 0-2 indicated a favorable functional outcome. Aneurysm occlusion was evaluated at the 6-month follow-up using the O'Kelly-Marotta (OKM) grading scale on digital subtraction angiography (DSA). Procedure-related complications, including in-stent stenosis (ISS), were systematically recorded.

RESULTS: All 29 aneurysms were successfully treated with FD, with no technical failures, in-stent thrombosis, cerebral hemorrhage, or ischemic events observed during the perioperative period. No patients developed new neurological deficits before discharge. All patients were followed up via telephone and outpatient visits after discharge. Six-month angiographic follow-up was performed in all 29 patients by DSA. The follow-up duration ranged from 6 to 43.2 months. At the final follow-up, one patient developed vertigo and a transient episode of left limb weakness more than 2 months after treatment. The mRS score was 0 in 28 patients and 1 in one patient. The 6-month angiographic outcomes were: OKM Grade A in 1 patient (3.4%), Grade B in 5 (17.3%), Grade C in 7 (24.1%), and Grade D in 16 (55.2%). ISS was observed in 3 patients (10.3%): one moderate proximal, one moderate mid-stent, and one diffuse severe stenosis. The overall procedure-related complication rate was 3.4% (1/29), with a mortality rate of 0%. The probability of achieving complete occlusion was >88.8% for necks ≤ 3.0 mm, compared to >53.3% for necks between 3.0-5.0 mm.

CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that the use of FDs is an effective and safe therapeutic option for MCA bifurcation aneurysms. A neck diameter ≤ 5.0 mm was associated with a higher likelihood of complete occlusion; this association requires external validation.
englishSummary: PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of flow diverters (FDs) for the treatment of middle cerebral artery (MCA) bifurcation aneurysms. METHODS: This retrospective, dual-center study enrolled 29 patients with unruptured MCA bifurcation aneurysms treated with flow diverters (FDs) between January 2021 and December 2024. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS), where scores of 0-2 indicated a favorable functional outcome.

title: Pipeline embolization device with adjunctive coiling for ruptured blood blister-like aneurysms: a multicenter study focusing on Hunt-Hess grade I-III patients.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood blister-like aneurysms (BBAs) of the internal carotid artery are rare and inherently unstable lesions that carry a high risk of rebleeding. Evidence regarding the outcomes of Pipeline embolization device (PED)-assisted coiling specifically in patients with mild-to-moderate neurological deficits (Hunt-Hess grade I-III) remains limited.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study, conducted at three comprehensive stroke centers between January 2018 and December 2023, included 28 consecutive patients with ruptured ICA BBAs. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of PED combined with adjunctive coil embolization using a deliberate loose-scaffolding strategy.

RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in 100% of cases. Immediate complete angiographic occlusion (modified Raymond-Roy class I) was observed in 67.9% (19/28), increasing to 75.0% (21/28) overall at 12 months and reaching 95.5% (21/22) among those with available imaging follow-up. Notably, all seven patients with residual neck filling on immediate postoperative angiography who completed follow-up subsequently achieved complete occlusion. Favorable clinical outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) was recorded in 92.9% (26/28) at last follow-up. Perioperative complications occurred in 39.3% (11/28), predominantly neurological, including symptomatic vasospasm (21.4%, 6/28) and cerebral infarction (14.3%, 4/28); perioperative mortality was 3.6% (1/28).

CONCLUSION: PED-assisted coil embolization with a loose-scaffolding strategy is technically feasible and may yield favorable outcomes in selected patients with mild-to-moderate neurologic deficits. However, given the retrospective, single-arm design and modest sample size, these results are hypothesis-generating; prospective comparative studies are warranted.

Evidence regarding the outcomes of Pipeline embolization device (PED)-assisted coiling specifically in patients with mild-to-moderate neurological deficits (Hunt-Hess grade I-III) remains limited. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study, conducted at three comprehensive stroke centers between January 2018 and December 2023, included 28 consecutive patients with ruptured ICA BBAs.

title: "Inflammation-Thrombosis Dissociation": a retrospective study of early DVT differences after UKA between Han Chinese and Tibetan patients at high altitude.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the incidence of early lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) after unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) between Han Chinese and Tibetan patients at high altitude, to analyze the relationships of inflammatory, hematologic, and coagulation indices with DVT, and to explore whether an "inflammation-thrombosis dissociation" phenomenon exists across ethnic groups.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 147 patients who underwent primary medial UKA at the Affiliated Hospital of Qinghai University (altitude 2,261 m) between March 2024 and June 2026, including 93 Tibetan and 54 Han Chinese patients. All patients received a standardized perioperative management protocol, including postoperative aspirin 100 mg once daily for venous thrombosis prophylaxis, and underwent bilateral lower-extremity venous color Doppler ultrasonography on postoperative days 2-3. Demographic characteristics, platelet count, hemoglobin, D-dimer, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, and aggregate index of systemic inflammation were collected. Propensity score matching was used to control differences in age, sex, and body mass index, and Firth logistic regression was used to analyze factors associated with DVT.

RESULTS: Among the 147 patients, 14 developed postoperative DVT, for an overall incidence of 9.52%. The DVT incidence was 4.30% (4/93) in Tibetan patients, lower than the 18.52% (10/54) observed in Han Chinese patients (P = 0.007). Platelet count, D-dimer, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, and aggregate index of systemic inflammation were all higher in Tibetan than in Han Chinese patients; however, these higher values did not correspond to a higher DVT incidence. After 1:1 matching for age, sex, and body mass index, 16 matched pairs were obtained; DVT incidences were 18.8% in Han Chinese patients and 0% in Tibetan patients. The difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.250), although the direction of the association was consistent with that before matching. Firth penalized-likelihood logistic regression showed that increasing age was associated with higher odds of DVT in Model 2 (OR = 1.110, 95% CI: 1.028-1.211, P = 0.007). In the primary model adjusted for age and BMI (Model 3), Tibetan ethnicity was associated with lower odds of DVT than Han Chinese ethnicity (OR = 0.206, 95% CI: 0.038-0.948, P = 0.042). However, this association was no longer statistically significant after further adjustment for sex (Model 4: OR = 0.243, 95% CI: 0.040-1.376, P = 0.109). In exploratory models separately incorporating postoperative platelet count, D-dimer, systemic immune-inflammation index, or aggregate index of systemic inflammation (Models 5-8), the association between ethnicity and DVT remained statistically significant (all P < 0.05), whereas none of these laboratory indices showed a statistically significant association with DVT (all P > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Among high-altitude UKA patients receiving a uniform aspirin prophylaxis regimen, Han Chinese patients had a higher incidence of early postoperative DVT than Tibetan patients. Although Tibetan patients had higher platelet counts and composite inflammatory indices, these measures did not increase in parallel with DVT events, suggesting a possible dissociation between inflammatory phenotype and clinical thrombotic risk among different ethnic groups at high altitude. Age and ethnicity were relatively stable DVT-associated factors in this cohort, whereas platelet count, D-dimer, and platelet-inflammation composite indices were insufficient to explain the between-ethnicity difference in risk. Given the single-center retrospective design and the limited number of outcome events and matched patients, these findings require further validation in multicenter, large-sample prospective studies.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: To compare the incidence of early lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) after unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) between Han Chinese and Tibetan patients at high altitude, to analyze the relationships of inflammatory, hematologic, and coagulation indices with DVT, and to explore whether an "inflammation-thrombosis dissociation" phenomenon exists across ethnic groups. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 147 patients who underwent primary medial UKA at the Affiliated Hospital of Qinghai University (altitude 2,261 m) between March 2024 and June 2026, including 93 Tibetan and 54 Han Chinese patients. All patients received a standardized perioperative management protocol, including postoperative aspirin 100 mg once daily for venous thrombosis prophylaxis, and underwent bilateral lower-extremity venous color Doppler ultrasonography on postoperative days 2-3.

title: Evaluation of Total Patent Branch Vessel Ostial Area at Preoperative CT Angiography for Predicting Type II Endoleak after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair.
abstract: Background Type II endoleak (T2EL) is a common complication after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) that may lead to aneurysm sac enlargement. Although guideline-based criteria are used to identify high-risk patients, their predictive accuracy remains limited. Purpose To evaluate the predictive value of preoperative total branch vessel ostial area at CT angiography (CTA) for T2EL after EVAR. Materials and Methods This single-center retrospective study included patients undergoing EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) between January 2010 and December 2020. After exclusion of other endoleak types, CTA-derived anatomic parameters and outcomes were compared by isolated T2EL status. Total branch vessel ostial area was evaluated using prespecified Cox models and Cox-least absolute shrinkage and selection operator analysis. Discrimination and reproducibility were assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, intraclass correlation coefficients, and Bland-Altman analysis. Results Of 216 patients in this study (mean age, 66 years ± 7.6 [SD]; 190 male; median follow-up, 4.7 years), 86 (39.8%) developed T2EL. Total branch vessel ostial area showed excellent reproducibility (intraclass correlation coefficients, 0.98-1.00) and was larger in patients with T2EL than in those without T2EL (median, 24.5 vs 11.7 mm2; P < .001). Sac enlargement was more frequent with T2EL (45.3% [39 of 86] vs 12.3% [16 of 130]; P < .001) and was associated with reintervention (hazard ratio [HR], 2.83; P = .003) but not overall survival (HR, 1.76; P = .28). In the fully adjusted Cox model, total branch vessel ostial area was associated with T2EL (HR, 1.06 per 1-mm2 increase [95% CI: 1.04, 1.08]; P < .001). Total branch ostial area showed better discrimination for T2EL than guideline-based criteria (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.82 vs 0.64; P < .001), with a Youden index-derived cutoff of 15.55 mm2. Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a positive continuous association in T2EL risk with increasing ostial area (P < .001). Conclusion Preoperative CTA-derived total branch vessel ostial area outperformed conventional branch diameter and count criteria for predicting T2EL in patients after EVAR for infrarenal AAA. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Liddell in this issue.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound for the detection of acute aortic syndrome in the emergency department: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute aortic syndromes (AAS) are a group of aortic disorders with a wide range of presentations that are easily misdiagnosed in the emergency department (ED). The 2024 European Society of Cardiology Guidelines recommended focused transthoracic echocardiography as the first-line imaging tool for the detection of aortic dissection, but the performance of point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in detecting AAS in ED varies considerably in the existing literature. We aim to gather and synthesize existing studies to provide a more comprehensive overview of the diagnostic accuracy and value of POCUS for the detection of AAS and its generalizability in the ED setting. METHODS: Ovid MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies published from 1 January 2000 to 21 July 2025. Diagnostic accuracy studies of POCUS in the ED for the detection of AAS were included. For included studies, the diagnostic accuracy of POCUS for detecting AAS was revealed by calculating the sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative likelihood ratio, and diagnostic odds ratio, with 95% credible intervals (CrI). The diagnostic performance of POCUS was evaluated by summary receiver operator curve (SROC). RESULTS: A total of 4,855 patients from seven studies were included in the meta-analysis. For any sonographic signs for detecting AAS, the pooled sensitivity and specificity of POCUS were 88.3% (95%CrI: 85.1% -91.2%) and 80.3% (95%CrI: 63.4%-92.9%), respectively. The area under the SROC of any sonographic signs for detecting AAS was 0.91 (95%CrI: 0.65-0.96). CONCLUSION: This systematic review provides support that POCUS may be a useful early imaging tool for ruling in AAS in the ED due to its high specificity for direct sonographic sign. While the overall certainty of evidence is moderate to low, larger-scale prospective studies on the use of POCUS with other diagnostic tools for detecting AAS are necessary in ED settings.

title: [Value of a CT angiography-based deep learning model for differentiating SVS grade Ⅱ and grade Ⅲ blunt thoracic aortic injury: a retrospective multicenter staged study].
abstract: Objectives: To develop a segmentation-guided multitask deep learning model for Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) grades Ⅰ to Ⅳ classification of blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI) and validate its clinical utility for differentiating SVS grades Ⅱ and Ⅲ. Methods: This is a retrospective case series study. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) data were collected from 317 patients with BTAI at 12 hospitals in China, including the First Medical Center of Chinese People's Liberation Army General Hospital, West China Hospital of Sichuan University, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University, and other local hospitals, between January 2006 and May 2026. The cohort included 258 male and 59 female patients, with an age of (54.8±15.3) years (range:16 to 92 years). The 253-patient development cohort was divided using a patient-level random split stratified by SVS injury grade and source center at an approximate ratio of 8∶2 into a training set of 202 patients and an internal validation set of 51 patients. The 64 BTAI cases from the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University were locked in advance as an independent external test set. The model consisted of a shared encoder, a lesion-segmentation branch, and a mask-guided classification branch. The primary outcomes were the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and grade Ⅲ sensitivity for differentiating SVS grade Ⅱ (intramural hematoma) from grade Ⅲ (pseudoaneurysm) in the external test set. Secondary outcomes included segmentation, automated measurements, and offline reader-study results. Results: The internal validation set covered SVS grades Ⅰ to Ⅳ, with an overall grading accuracy of 92.2% (47/51) and a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.919. The external test set included 31 SVS grade Ⅱ (intramural hematoma) cases and 33 SVS grade Ⅲ (pseudoaneurysm) cases. The model had an AUC of 0.968 (95%CI:0.924 to 0.996), an accuracy of 92.2% (59/64), grade Ⅲ sensitivity of 93.9% (31/33), and grade Ⅱ specificity of 90.3% (28/31); two grade Ⅲ cases were misclassified as grade Ⅱ. The automated segmentation success rate was 96.9% (62/64), the overall lesion Dice similarity coefficient was 0.872±0.072 (range:0.46 to 0.99), and model inference time per case was (15.4±2.4) s (range:10.8 to 22.6 s). In the fixed-sequence reader study, six junior physicians had higher grade Ⅱ/Ⅲ accuracy and grade Ⅲ sensitivity and shorter interpretation times during the artificial intelligence-assisted phase than during the unaided phase. Conclusions: The segmentation-guided CTA deep learning model developed in this study performed BTAI lesion segmentation, SVS grading, and measurement of key morphologic parameters, and maintained good discrimination between SVS grades Ⅱ and Ⅲ in the independent external test set. Model assistance may help reduce missed grade Ⅲ cases by junior physicians and shorten interpretation time, thereby supporting standardized imaging assessment of BTAI.

Methods: This is a retrospective case series study. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) data were collected from 317 patients with BTAI at 12 hospitals in China, including the First Medical Center of Chinese People's Liberation Army General Hospital, West China Hospital of Sichuan University, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University, and other local hospitals, between January 2006 and May 2026.

title: Effect of a Nurse-Driven Early Mobilization Protocol on Biomarker Levels and Incidence of Deep Vein Thrombosis After Lower Extremity Fracture Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of a nurse-driven early mobilization protocol on the incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), biomarker levels, and clinical outcomes in patients after lower extremity fracture surgery.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 205 patients who underwent surgery for traumatic unilateral lower extremity fractures (January 2023 to June 2025). Patients were divided into a control group (conventional care, n = 107) and an early mobilization group (nurse-driven protocol, n = 98) using July 2024 as the implementation cutoff. Outcomes included postoperative DVT incidence, changes in D-dimer and C-reactive protein (CRP), bed rest duration, pain scores, length of stay, and complications. Repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) compared biomarker changes; binary logistic regression identified DVT risk factors.

RESULTS: The early mobilization group had a significantly lower incidence of postoperative DVT than the control group (7.14% vs. 19.63%, P = 0.009), with an absolute risk reduction of 12.49% and a relative risk reduction of 63.6%. Repeated-measures ANOVA showed significant between-group effects (F = 22.33, P < 0.001) and interaction effects (F = 6.36, P < 0.001) for CRP levels. After Bonferroni correction, the early mobilization group had significantly lower D-dimer and CRP levels at 1 week postoperatively and at discharge than the control group (P < 0.0125). The early mobilization group also had significantly better outcomes in terms of bed rest duration (5.86 ± 1.69 days vs. 6.38 ± 1.54 days, P = 0.021), numerical rating scale score on postoperative day 3 (3.27 ± 1.15 vs. 4.54 ± 1.47, P < 0.001), and length of hospital stay (median 11.00 days vs. 13.00 days, P < 0.001), as well as a lower complication rate (6.12% vs. 14.95%, P = 0.041). Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified the early mobilization protocol (odds ratio [OR] = 0.27, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.10-0.73, P = 0.009), age (OR = 1.05, 95% CI: 1.02-1.08, P = 0.001), and postoperative day 1 D-dimer level (OR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.05-1.47, P = 0.011) as independent factors influencing postoperative DVT.

CONCLUSION: A nurse-driven early mobilization protocol effectively reduces the incidence of DVT after lower extremity fracture surgery, improves coagulation and inflammatory biomarker levels, shortens hospital stay, and does not increase complication risks. The protocol is safe and feasible and can be recommended as an adjunctive measure for venous thromboembolism prevention after lower extremity fracture surgery.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of a nurse-driven early mobilization protocol on the incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), biomarker levels, and clinical outcomes in patients after lower extremity fracture surgery. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 205 patients who underwent surgery for traumatic unilateral lower extremity fractures (January 2023 to June 2025). Patients were divided into a control group (conventional care, n = 107) and an early mobilization group (nurse-driven protocol, n = 98) using July 2024 as the implementation cutoff.

title: Functional Vulnerability and Long-Term Mortality in Adults with Ankle-Brachial Index-Defined Peripheral Artery Disease: An NHANES Cohort Study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Functional limitations are common in peripheral artery disease (PAD), but the association of a brief self-reported functional-burden measure with objectively defined PAD and long-term mortality remains incompletely characterized.

METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2004 participants aged ≥ 40 years with ankle-brachial index (ABI), physical functioning, and linked mortality data. PAD was defined as minimum ABI ≤ 0.90. An NHANES-derived functional vulnerability index (NFVI; range 0-4) was constructed from difficulty walking a quarter mile, walking up 10 steps, stooping/crouching/kneeling, and standing for long periods. NFVI was intended as a brief functional-burden measure rather than a diagnostic frailty instrument. Survey-weighted models evaluated PAD status, NFVI, and mortality, with validated modified cardiovascular health (mCVH) used for additional adjustment.

RESULTS: The PAD NFVI cohort included 462 participants and 375 deaths. PAD was associated with high NFVI after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and mCVH (odds ratio [OR] 1.748, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.218-2.510; P = 0.005). In PAD participants, each 1-point higher NFVI was associated with all-cause mortality after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and minimum ABI (hazards ratio [HR] 1.095, 95% CI 1.017-1.179; P = 0.017). After additional mCVH adjustment, the continuous association was attenuated (HR 1.075, 95% CI 0.993-1.165; P = 0.075), whereas high NFVI remained associated with mortality (HR 1.346, 95% CI 1.026-1.767; P = 0.032). Complete-case selection was substantial (462/647 PAD participants), with marked differences between included and excluded participants, particularly in age, potentially limiting generalizability.

CONCLUSION: Functional vulnerability was more common among adults with ABI-defined PAD and was associated with long-term all-cause mortality. These findings demonstrate an epidemiologic association rather than the clinical utility, validation, or incremental prognostic value of NFVI and do not establish a clinically meaningful NFVI mortality threshold. Prospective PAD-specific validation and comparison with established frailty measures are required before clinical use.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Functional limitations are common in peripheral artery disease (PAD), but the association of a brief self-reported functional-burden measure with objectively defined PAD and long-term mortality remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2004 participants aged ≥ 40 years with ankle-brachial index (ABI), physical functioning, and linked mortality data. PAD was defined as minimum ABI ≤ 0.90.

title: Effects of Endovascular Repair Timing on the Outcomes of Type B Aortic Dissection in an Asian Multicenter Cohort.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study assessed thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) timing and its impact on outcomes in type B aortic dissection (TBAD).

METHOD: This multicenter retrospective study included 247 patients who underwent TEVAR for TBAD between 2011 and 2018, using data from the Chang Gung Research Database. Primary outcomes were in-hospital and postdischarge mortality.

RESULTS: The study included 47, 122, and 78 patients with hyperacute (<1 day), acute/subacute (1-90 days), and chronic (>90 days) TBAD, respectively. Chronic TBAD had more aortic expansion before TEVAR (0% vs. 6.6% vs. 17.6%; P = 0.001). In-hospital mortality was highest in hyperacute TBAD (17%) and lowest in chronic TBAD (6.4%; adjusted P for trend = 0.036); conversely, long-term mortality was highest in chronic TBAD (12.3%) and lowest in hyperacute TBAD (0%; adjusted P for trend = 0.017). A restricted cubic spline model showed that delayed intervention beyond 90 days is associated with increasing long-term mortality risk. Among secondary outcomes, delayed TEVAR was associated with more aortic, cardiovascular, infection-related deaths, and residual aneurysms (adjusted P for trend = 0.039, 0.012, 0.048, and 0.006, respectively).

CONCLUSION: TEVAR may lead to unfavorable outcomes in hyperacute and chronic TBAD. Delayed TEVAR in chronic TBAD is associated with adverse aortic remodeling and rising long-term mortality. TEVAR before the chronic phase could be considered to improve short-term and long-term outcomes.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: This study assessed thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) timing and its impact on outcomes in type B aortic dissection (TBAD). METHOD: This multicenter retrospective study included 247 patients who underwent TEVAR for TBAD between 2011 and 2018, using data from the Chang Gung Research Database. Primary outcomes were in-hospital and postdischarge mortality.

title: Ultrasound-guided selective nerve block promotes perioperative vascular remodeling and early maturation of radiocephalic arteriovenous fistulas.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for maintenance hemodialysis, but its successful maturation depends on adequate perioperative vascular remodeling. We evaluated whether ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB) promotes vascular remodeling and improves AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation.

METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis based on a prospectively-maintained single-center vascular access clinical follow-up database. We included 163 patients with stage 5 chronic kidney disease undergoing primary radiocephalic AVF creation between January 2023 and January 2024. Patients received ultrasound-guided SNB (n = 72) or local infiltration anesthesia (LA, n = 91). Perioperative changes in radial artery and cephalic vein diameters were evaluated, postoperative brachial artery blood flow was recorded, and AVF maturation was assessed at 1, 2, and 3 months. Linear mixed-effects models and multivariable logistic regression were used for analysis.

RESULTS: Compared with LA, SNB significantly increased radial artery and cephalic vein diameters after anesthesia, whereas both vessels constricted in the LA group (both P < .001). Linear mixed-effects analysis demonstrated significant time effects and group-by-time interactions for both vessels, whereas a significant group effect was observed only for the cephalic vein (all P < .001). Postoperative brachial artery blood flow was significantly greater in the SNB group (P < .001). The 2-month AVF maturation rate was significantly higher in the SNB group than in the LA group (60% vs 35%; P = .002), whereas no between-group differences were observed at 1 or 3 months. Younger age, larger preoperative radial artery diameter, and SNB were independent predictors of AVF maturation.

CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided SNB promotes perioperative vascular remodeling, increases postoperative blood flow, and independently facilitates early AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation. These findings support SNB as a promising perioperative strategy to optimize vascular access outcomes in patients undergoing AVF creation.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for maintenance hemodialysis, but its successful maturation depends on adequate perioperative vascular remodeling. We evaluated whether ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB) promotes vascular remodeling and improves AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation. METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis based on a prospectively-maintained single-center vascular access clinical follow-up database.

title: Neutrophil extracellular traps drive immunoinflammatory remodeling in abdominal aortic aneurysm: from inflammatory amplification to precision therapy.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a chronic vascular disorder characterized by progressive aortic wall dilation, extracellular matrix degradation, and an increased risk of catastrophic rupture. Currently, no effective pharmacological therapy is available to prevent or slow AAA progression. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have emerged as a critical pathological platform linking dysregulated innate immunity to vascular structural deterioration. In the AAA microenvironment, local inflammation, oxidative stress, metabolic disturbances, altered mechanical forces, and platelet activation collectively contribute to the induction of NETosis. Persistent NET formation promotes immunoinflammatory remodeling of the aortic wall by activating inflammatory sensing pathways, including TLR9, cGAS-STING, and NLRP3, modulating macrophage responses, inducing vascular smooth muscle cell ferroptosis and phenotypic switching, and exacerbating proteolytic degradation, oxidative injury, and immunothrombotic responses. During disease progression, NETs may transition from early drivers of inflammatory amplification to sustained regulators of vascular remodeling, while in advanced AAA they may synergize with intraluminal thrombus formation and structural destabilization to accelerate disease progression. Circulating NET-associated biomarkers represent promising candidates for complementing conventional imaging-based risk assessment; however, their specificity and predictive value require further validation. Therapeutic strategies targeting PAD4-mediated NET formation, the oxidative metabolic environment, NET-associated effector molecules, DNase I-mediated NET degradation, and nucleic acid sensing pathways have demonstrated potential in preclinical studies. This review systematically summarizes the emerging roles of NETs in AAA pathogenesis and discusses future precision strategies integrating biomarkers, multi-omics profiling, and imaging-based risk stratification with stage-specific therapeutic interventions.

Currently, no effective pharmacological therapy is available to prevent or slow AAA progression. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have emerged as a critical pathological platform linking dysregulated innate immunity to vascular structural deterioration.

title: Elastography and Vector Flow Imaging Detect Arteriovenous Fistula Stenosis Independent of Luminal Diameter.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the diagnostic value of multimodal ultrasound (US)-including 2-dimensional (2D) US, sound touch elastography (STE), and vector flow imaging (VFI)-for the identification of functional and biomechanical abnormalities indicative of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) stenosis or occlusion in hemodialysis patients.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 37 hemodialysis patients with AVFs, divided into normal (n = 20) and dysfunction (n = 17) groups based on digital subtraction angiography (DSA) or clinical/US criteria. For the dysfunction group, AVF stenosis was defined as >50% luminal diameter reduction on DSA, and occlusion was defined as complete absence of flow. For the normal group, dysfunction was excluded by clinical examination (thrill/bruit) and normal duplex parameters. All patients underwent 2D US, STE, and VFI examinations. Key parameters measured included vessel diameter, elasticity (kPa), blood flow velocities, turbulence (Tur) index, and wall shear stress (WSS). Statistical comparisons were made between groups.

RESULTS: No significant differences were found in vessel diameter or intima status between groups. However, the stenosis/occlusion group exhibited significantly lower mean blood flow, peak systolic/end-diastolic velocities, and WSS, along with higher resistance index and vessel wall stiffness (STE mean, 30.35 kPa [SD ± 11.65] vs 20.7 kPa [SD ± 7.52]; P < .01). VFI revealed reduced blood flow velocity, Tur, and WSS in dysfunctional AVFs (all P < .01).

CONCLUSIONS: Multimodal US integrating 2D US, STE, and VFI provides a comprehensive assessment of AVF structure and function, detecting functional and biomechanical abnormalities associated with AVF stenosis or occlusion.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 37 hemodialysis patients with AVFs, divided into normal (n = 20) and dysfunction (n = 17) groups based on digital subtraction angiography (DSA) or clinical/US criteria. For the dysfunction group, AVF stenosis was defined as >50% luminal diameter reduction on DSA, and occlusion was defined as complete absence of flow.

title: Snapshots of ATP-driven substrate translocation by the mitochondrial AAA+ protease AFG3L2.
abstract: AFG3L2, located in the mitochondrial inner membrane, is an ATP-fueled protease responsible for protein degradation, and its dysfunction has been implicated in multiple neurodegenerative disorders. However, the structural basis underlying its ATP-driven substrate translocation remains incompletely understood. Here, we purified full-length human AFG3L2 and determined its cryo-EM structures in four distinct conformational states (Con1-Con4), revealing substrate engagement in the core catalytic domain despite weak EM density for its transmembrane domain. These structures display an asymmetric spiral-staircase architecture in which the six protomers are arranged around a central pore that accommodates a polypeptide substrate. The four conformational states jointly reveal a substrate translocation mechanism in which ATP binding by the uppermost protomer promotes substrate engagement, whereas ATP hydrolysis by the lowermost ATP-bound protomer leads to substrate release. Our findings provide snapshots of ATP-driven substrate translocation by AFG3L2 and refine the hand-over-hand translocation mechanism by revealing substrate capture and release during an ordered ATPase cycle.

title: Predictive value of combined cerebral blood volume index and systemic inflammation indices for 90-day functional outcomes following endovascular treatment in patients with acute ischemic stroke and proximal large vessel occlusion: machine learning model construction and population attributable fraction analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We investigated whether the cerebral blood volume (CBV) index and pretreatment systemic inflammatory indices (SIIs) provide complementary prognostic information for 90-day functional outcomes after successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for anterior circulation large vessel occlusion and evaluated the advantages of machine learning models in terms of prognostic outcomes and quantified adverse outcomes using the population attributable fraction (PAF).

METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation. SIIs were calculated from the first venous sample obtained at presentation, before intravenous thrombolysis, and before arterial puncture for EVT. Multivariate logistic regression and eight predictive algorithms were evaluated. PAF estimates were considered exploratory.

RESULTS: Among 474 patients, 41.6% and 28.5% achieved favorable and excellent outcomes, respectively. Higher CBV indices were more frequent among patients with favorable outcomes, whereas higher inflammatory indices were associated with worse outcomes. Logistic regression showed the highest AUC for mRS 0-2 (0.868, 95% CI 0.806-0.929), while SVM had the highest AUC for mRS 0-1 (0.839, 95% CI 0.764-0.915). The external validation AUCs were 0.816 and 0.802. PAF analysis indicated that improving the CBV index increased favorable and excellent outcomes by 97.2% and 74.8%, respectively, whereas reducing inflammatory overactivation improved them by 22.4%-39.7% and 51.2%-59.5%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Baseline CBV index and pretreatment SII values provided complementary prognostic information after successful EVT. However, prospective validation in a broader population is required before clinical implementation.

METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation.

title: Cause-Specific Endovascular Thrombectomy Time Windows in Basilar Artery Occlusion: ATTENTION Trial Post Hoc Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) outperforms best medical treatment (BMT) for basilar artery occlusion (BAO), but the influence of stroke cause on the time sensitivity of EVT remains unclear. We hypothesized nonatherosclerotic BAO would require earlier EVT, whereas atherosclerotic BAO-with chronic stenosis and more robust collaterals-would retain EVT benefit in extended windows. We conducted a post hoc 3-way interaction analysis of the ATTENTION trial (Trial of Endovascular Treatment of Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion) to explore cause-specific EVT time patterns.

METHODS: Using randomized ATTENTION trial data (36 Chinese centers, 2021-2022), patients were stratified by onset-to-puncture time (<6 versus ≥6 hours) and TOAST (Trial of ORG 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment) cause (atherosclerotic: large-artery atherosclerosis; nonatherosclerotic: cardioembolism/undetermined/other causes). The primary outcome was 90-day favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 0-3), with relative risk as the primary estimand; the 3-way interaction was tested via joint Wald test. A weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis served as an exploratory tool, with multivariable regression adjusting for confounders.

RESULTS: Among 340 patients (226 EVT+BMT, 114 BMT), for onset-to-puncture time <6 hours, patients with nonatherosclerotic BAO who received EVT achieved a significantly higher favorable outcome rate (46.7% versus 20.4%; relative risk, 2.29 [95% CI, 1.25-4.18]; P=0.007); the atherosclerotic group showed numerical outcome benefit (40.4% versus 26.1%, P=0.259). For onset-to-puncture time ≥6 hours, the numerical benefit in the atherosclerotic group increased from 14.3% to 30.6% (56.9% versus 26.3%; P=0.199), accompanied by ordinal modified Rankin Scale score improvement (common odds ratio, 3.30 [95% CI, 1.13-9.62]; P=0.029) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score reduction; the benefit in the nonatherosclerotic group decreased from 26.3% to 17.8% with loss of significance (39.5% versus 21.7%, P=0.341). The treatment time×cause interaction was not significant (P=0.662). The weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis identified a provisional 5.3-hour reference point in nonatherosclerotic BAO.

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with nonatherosclerotic BAO, atherosclerotic BAO appears less time-sensitive, potentially retaining EVT responsiveness over longer windows. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

title: Postoperative recruitment and remodeling of middle meningeal artery collaterals in adult moyamoya disease: implications for preservation during combined revascularization.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The middle meningeal artery (MMA) may provide pre-existing transdural flow and postoperative collateral recruitment in adult moyamoya disease (MMD). We evaluated MMA remodeling, recruitment, and the safety relevance of preserving visible branches during combined revascularization.

METHODS: This retrospective hemisphere-level study included 110 operated hemispheres from 85 adults undergoing superficial temporal artery-middle cerebral artery bypass with encephaloduromyosynangiosis. Preoperative angiography showed visible MMA collaterals in 38 hemispheres and none in 72. Outcomes included vessel diameters, MMA caliber change ratio (MMA-CCR), Matsushima grade, and perioperative infarction. Groups were further classified by intraoperative MMA preservation or injury and by postoperative recruitment.

RESULTS: Hemispheres with visible preoperative collaterals had more advanced Suzuki stages (P < 0.001), larger postoperative MMA diameters (P = 0.006), and smaller postoperative donor superficial temporal artery diameters (P < 0.001). Among collateral-absent hemispheres, 56/72 (77.8%) developed postoperative MMA collaterals. Recruited hemispheres had better Matsushima grades (P = 0.001), larger preoperative (3.05 ± 1.14 vs 2.23 ± 1.19 mm; P = 0.016) and postoperative MMA diameters (P < 0.001), and higher MMA-CCR values (P < 0.001). Perioperative infarction occurred in 3/10 hemispheres with MMA injury and 0/28 with preservation (P = 0.014); this three-event association was exploratory.

CONCLUSION: The MMA showed postoperative recruitment and caliber remodeling. Visible branches should be preserved when technically feasible, although the observed association between injury and infarction requires validation.

We evaluated MMA remodeling, recruitment, and the safety relevance of preserving visible branches during combined revascularization. METHODS: This retrospective hemisphere-level study included 110 operated hemispheres from 85 adults undergoing superficial temporal artery-middle cerebral artery bypass with encephaloduromyosynangiosis.

title: Characterizing the Thrombotic Spectrum and Clinical Phenotypes of Tranexamic Acid-Associated Adverse Events: A Pharmacovigilance Study Based on the FAERS Database.
abstract: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is widely used to reduce bleeding in surgical, trauma, obstetric, and gynecological settings. However, concerns remain regarding TXA-associated thrombotic adverse events, and their phenotypic heterogeneity and clinical severity have not been comprehensively characterized. This study investigated TXA-associated thrombotic events using the Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) from 2004Q1 to 2026Q1. Thrombotic adverse events were identified using the Standardized MedDRA Query (SMQ) "Embolic and thrombotic events" and evaluated by disproportionality analysis based on reporting odds ratios (RORs). Qualifying thrombotic events were assigned to the SMQ vessel-type subgroups-arterial, vessel-type unspecified/mixed, and venous-and demographic characteristics, indications, clinical outcomes and time-to-onset were compared across subgroups; signal strength was further related to clinical severity. In all, 515 thrombotic cases associated with TXA and 26 selected thrombotic terms were found (arterial, 157; mixed, 168; venous, 190). Venous thromboembolism-pulmonary embolism (n = 128, ROR 13.94) and deep vein thrombosis (n = 58, ROR 9.09)-is the most frequent type and brings about the most severe and fatal consequences (death reported in 16.8% of venous versus 2.5% of arterial reports), whereas the strongest disproportionality signals were observed for rare site-specific events such as ovarian vein thrombosis (ROR 352.95) and cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (ROR 118.35). The three subgroups differed markedly in demographic and clinical characteristics: venous events occurred predominantly in women (73.7%) treated for menorrhagia (35.3%), whereas arterial events arose mainly in surgical or procedural settings (intravenous route 36.3%; surgery/prophylaxis 19.1%) and presented earliest after exposure [median time-to-onset (TTO) 0 versus 7 days]. Signal strength was not concordant with clinical severity across the thrombotic spectrum. These findings provide a deeper understanding of the thrombotic safety of TXA, indicate that the clinical background may influence the phenotypic differences among the different thrombotic types, and emphasize the necessity of enhanced attention and risk stratification in high-risk groups.

title: Initial Direct Oral Anticoagulants Versus Warfarin After Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Target Trial Emulation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vitamin K antagonists have traditionally been used after cerebral venous thrombosis, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly prescribed. Whether DOACs are noninferior to warfarin for preventing 1-year symptomatic recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a registry-based target trial emulation in a bidirectional multicenter Chinese cerebral venous thrombosis registry (retrospective phase, 2015-2022; prospective phase, 2023-2025). Eligible patients were adults with imaging-confirmed cerebral venous thrombosis who initiated either a DOAC or warfarin within 30 days after diagnosis. Time zero was the date of the first oral anticoagulant prescription. The primary efficacy outcome was symptomatic recurrent VTE within 1 year. Propensity score overlap weighting was used, and weighted Fine-Gray models treated death as a competing event. The clinically acceptable noninferiority margin was defined as an absolute increase of 1.5 percentage points in 1-year recurrent VTE risk, corresponding approximately to a relative margin of 1.50 for the primary Fine-Gray analysis.

RESULTS: Among 2476 eligible patients, 942 initiated a DOAC (rivaroxaban, n=701; dabigatran, n=121; apixaban, n=113; edoxaban, n=7) and 1534 initiated warfarin. Within 1 year, symptomatic recurrent VTE occurred in 36 and 73 patients, respectively. The overlap-weighted 1-year recurrence risks were 3.74% and 5.47%, corresponding to a risk difference of -1.73 percentage points (95% CI, -3.76 to 0.30). DOAC treatment was associated with a lower subdistribution hazard ratio of 0.67 compared with that of warfarin ([95% CI, 0.37-1.21]; P=0.184), meeting the prespecified noninferiority criterion (P for noninferiority=0.004). Major bleeding was rare within 1 year (0 versus 1 patient). Clinical nonmajor bleeding occurred in 18 versus 34 patients, and any bleeding occurred in 48 versus 75 patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with cerebral venous thrombosis selected for oral anticoagulation, initial treatment with a DOAC met the noninferiority criterion relative to warfarin for the prevention of symptomatic recurrent VTE at 1 year. Findings regarding bleeding outcomes were exploratory and do not permit conclusions regarding comparative safety or equivalence.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Vitamin K antagonists have traditionally been used after cerebral venous thrombosis, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly prescribed. Whether DOACs are noninferior to warfarin for preventing 1-year symptomatic recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain. METHODS: We conducted a registry-based target trial emulation in a bidirectional multicenter Chinese cerebral venous thrombosis registry (retrospective phase, 2015-2022; prospective phase, 2023-2025).
